### Worth landing regardless

Genie **can police a vendored tree but cannot produce one**: `output.validate` needs zero core changes, while producing 55 files does not fit its 1-source→1-target model. A `validate` hook that recomputes a content hash against a megarepo-pinned source is a reusable "this file must match that repo" primitive, independent of vendoring.

Also established: `bundleDependencies` is not viable — `pnpm pack` hard-errors under isolated `nodeLinker`, and `bun install` fails to resolve an unpublished bundled dep. And Node subpath `imports` (`#vendor/…`) is the *only* workable specifier mechanism, since a package cannot alias a bare specifier to a path inside itself and `tsconfig` `paths` does not ship to consumers.

## Split out of this epic

This epic surfaced three things that are not part of the migration. They are tracked separately so this checklist stays a plan:

| Concern | Issue |
| --- | --- |
| Size-gated source-available licence across all packages; retire sponsorware DevTools | **#1511** |
| Five pre-existing devtools protocol defects found by modelling | **#1509** |
| `@livestore/devtools-web-common` npm-scope orphan | **#1510** |

Licensing decisions that constrain this epic (D2, D9) now live in #1511. The packaging fix there — `devtools-vite` and `devtools-react` currently publish with no `license` field — should land ahead of this migration, not after.

## Decisions (settled)

| # | Decision | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Both the plugin **and** the UI source move; the Chrome extension moves too | The producer is retired and the handoff repo can be archived |
| D2 | **Licence: LiveStore Community License 1.0** — size-gated source-available, whole system. Decided in **#1511**; this epic consumes it rather than owning it | Contrib becomes mixed-licence (`LSC-DQ2`). The packaging fix in #1511 LM0 should land **before** this migration |
| D3 | **Maximal lockstep.** Every npm package — core, contrib, and the three incoming devtools packages — publishes at one shared version. Version numbers stop carrying compatibility meaning anywhere | Upholds `0001-two-repo-composition` rather than carving it up, and deletes version-coupling machinery wholesale rather than adding a second versioning model |
| D4 | Core's devtools test suite **relocates to contrib** | Removes core's release-time dependency on a contrib publish |
| D5 | **Two consumption paths from one source.** `devtools-react` ships **TypeScript source**; `devtools-vite` compiles it at build time for the drop-in plugin, and consumers compile it directly when embedding devtools in their own app | Kills the dual-mode bundle resolution and the dead `release-metadata.json` payload |
| D6 | The "Certify DevTools artifact liveness" gate is replaced by an **exact-install boot gate** (pack → clean `npm install` → 35 s liveness), not deleted | Under D5 the resolution path changes; deleting the gate at the same moment would ship green-building, boot-broken packages |
| D7 | The Chrome zip ships from **contrib's** GitHub releases | Contrib CI has only `contents: read` + `id-token: write`; keeping the zip on core's release would mean granting a public repo `contents:write` on core. Under D3's lockstep, contrib's tag **is** core's version, so this is a **host swap only** — the three consumers keep the same `v${liveStoreVersion}` keying and asset filename; no URL resolver needed. Requires `contents: write` scoped to the uploading job (contrib is `contents: read` today). The extension's own CWS version is separate and must be monotonic |
| D8 | **One negotiated protocol, at one boundary.** Compatibility is negotiated only on the wire, and only for surfaces distributed **out-of-band** — installed and updated independently of the app (today the Chrome extension; tomorrow other browser extensions or a standalone devtools app) | Everything shipping together is compatible by construction. The single mechanism replaces version semantics currently smeared across npm pins, artifact metadata, `compatibleLivestore` ranges and the CWS version mapping. Fires `LS.SYS.DT-DQ1`, which is currently open |


## Honest costs of maximal lockstep (D3)

Recorded because the epic should not pretend these away:

- **`devtools-chrome` cannot be lockstepped at all** — it never reaches npm. Its binding to a core release is the protocol version, which is exactly what D8 is for. (`devtools-react` *can* be, since D5 makes it a published package.)
- **Decision `0002-devtools-artifact-cadence` is `status: accepted` and explicitly rejected** the option maximal lockstep is a stronger form of — "makes every LiveStore release a DevTools release". Superseding it is mandatory, not optional.
- **A devtools-only fix now costs a full release-group publish** across ~23 packages; conversely a core patch republishes devtools with an unchanged build under a new number.
- **The CWS monotonic-version constraint is unguarded.** The artifact check validates only that the ZIP *contains* a `manifest.json` — it never reads the version and nothing compares against the previous release. A non-monotonic Chrome version would surface as a store rejection **after** npm has published: a half-completed release. A monotonicity gate is a prerequisite, not a follow-up. Chrome's 4-integer format also cannot represent the semver space (`0.4.0-dev.24` and `0.4.0-rc.24` both map to `0.4.0.24`), so the mapping must be a decision, not a derivation.
- **A real consumer already needs a different pairing:** `vue-livestore@0.2.3` pins a complete `0.3.1` tree. Under "version numbers carry no compatibility meaning" it has no expressible way to state what it needs.
- **`@livestore/wa-sqlite` is a fork** with `1.0.5-dev.2` in the wild — a version that means something on the *upstream* lineage. Folding it into lockstep destroys that information.
- **`@livestore/effect-playwright` is already a carve-out** (`version 0.0.0, private: true`, in the changesets `ignore` list). Decide whether carve-outs are permitted in principle before calling the policy maximal.

## Complexity removed (the point of the epic)

Things that exist only because of the split, verified in-tree:

- `dist/release-metadata.json` — shipped in the package, **referenced by neither `plugin.js` nor the UI bundle**. Dead payload.
- `LSD_DEVTOOLS_LOCAL_PREVIEW` dual-mode resolution (source via `/@fs/` vs embedded `dist/devtools-bundle/`) — collapses to one mode under D5.
- The artifact metadata vocabulary — `artifactVersion`, `devtoolsBuildId`, `sourceRevision`, `compatibleLivestore`, `schemaVersion` — all producer-side, all gone. Protocol version becomes the only compat concept.
- The `@parcel/watcher` `packageExtensions` patch, declared at **three** sites (`genie/repo.ts`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml.genie.ts`, and the generated `pnpm-install-contract.json`). *Correction to the original framing:* the repack does **not** strip this dep — it spreads `pkg.dependencies` untouched. The patch compensates for the **prebuilt artifact's own `package.json` never declaring it**, a private-build packaging gap. So contrib's `devtools-vite/package.json` must declare `@parcel/watcher` explicitly. The genuinely repack-caused native handling is the runtime hand-copy in `devenv.nix`, which exists only because the tarball is installed outside pnpm's resolution.
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml.genie.ts` `strictPeerDependencies: false`, commented as relaxed *specifically* for devtools-vite — a re-tightening candidate.
- ~285 of `devenv.nix`'s 662 lines (**~43%**) — the repack exec, the 196-line certify-liveness block with its `hydrate_devtools_package` and platform-optional-dep copying, the task factory, and four `release:devtools-artifact:*` tasks.
- Contrib's `@livestore/devtools-vite` external pin `0.4.0-dev.25` in `adapter-node`, `devtools-expo` (peer), `tests/integration`, `tests/sync-provider`, and **9 hand-edited example `package.json` files** (examples have zero `.genie.ts`, so every bump is 9 manual edits today) — all become `workspace:*`.
- Contrib's `devenv.nix` `forbidden = ['devtools-web-common', …]` negative guard — premise expires once the devtools closure is genuinely in-repo.
- Core's `genie/external.ts` `LIVESTORE_RELEASE_VERSION` escape hatch for the devtools catalog entry — leaves contrib's side entirely.

## Blocker found during planning

**Deleting `scripts/src/commands/devtools-artifact.ts` would delete core's GitHub Release publishing *and* its git tagging.**

`publishChromeZipReleaseAsset` is the *only* code path in the repo running `gh release view` / `edit --notes-file` / `create` / `upload` (`devtools-artifact.ts:614`, `:627`, `:630`, `:640`). Verified twice independently; zero hits in the generated workflows, and `release.yml.genie.ts:767` is a comment documenting the dependency.

**The quieter half:** `gh release create v$version` is also core's **only git-tag creator**. A grep for `git tag` / `refs/tags` / `--tags` across core returns only ruleset schema literals in `scripts/src/commands/github.ts`, yet `v0.4.0` and the whole `v0.4.0-dev.*` series exist on the remote. Deleting the script silently stops tagging — no test catches that.

So core's Release page *and* its tags are side effects of the DevTools artifact publish. **~35 lines relocate** (`:596–607`, `:609–637`), not the whole block: `gh release upload` at `:640` does **not** relocate — under D7 the zip ships from contrib, so it has no core-side destination and dies with the script.

Three consumers read that Release: `tests/integration/scripts/download-chrome-extension.ts:39` (**functional** — matches the asset by name), the `adapter-web` log hint, and the install docs. Under D3's lockstep all three key the asset by `v${liveStoreVersion}`, and contrib's tag *is* core's version — so **D7 is a host swap only**, with version interpolation and filename unchanged. No URL resolver needed.

## Open questions

Licensing questions moved to #1511. What remains is migration-local; two are already resolved and kept for the record.

1. ~~D3 vs the lockstep decision~~ — **resolved (2026-07-27).** `0001-two-repo-composition` stands unamended: maximal lockstep for everything on npm (D3). The compatibility problem it cannot solve — a surface installed out-of-band from the app — is handled by one negotiated wire protocol instead (D8), not by a second versioning model. Measurement showed nothing real couples devtools to a core version, so lockstep costs nothing at the npm layer.
   **Accepted cost, stated plainly:** under lockstep a devtools-only fix requires bumping every package, i.e. a core release. The pre-migration artifact flow could ship devtools independently; that capability is deliberately traded away for the tooling simplification.
2. ~~The out-of-band protocol design (D8)~~ — **resolved by modelling (see above).** Keep the single-version strict-reject design; add per-namespace gating + connection epochs. The one remaining product question: **must a v(N-1) extension keep working after a protocol bump, or is "update your extension" acceptable?** The invariant suite cannot distinguish these — a version window costs one new `Pong` field and buys exactly one release of grace. Answering "update your extension" keeps the simpler design.
   *Superseded detail, kept for context:* The mechanism must be as small as possible while holding one invariant: never a half-working session. Constraints already verified:
   - `common/src/version.ts:12` — `supportedDevtoolsProtocolVersions` is a **single-element list**, so today any protocol bump hard-breaks every installed extension. A window of accepted versions is the minimum change that makes out-of-band distribution safe.
   - The Chrome manifest maps `0.4.0-dev.24` → `"0.4.0.24"`. A stable `0.4.0` maps *lower*, and Chrome requires strictly increasing versions — so the extension needs a monotonic scheme of its own regardless of D3.
   - Skew-test machinery exists on the **app** side only (`__LIVESTORE_DEVTOOLS_PROTOCOL_VERSION_OVERRIDE__`, used by `browser-extension.play.ts:81` / `web.play.ts:75`); there is no surface-side equivalent, so "old extension vs new core" is not currently testable.
   - The core↔extension contract is **duplicated string literals with no shared type** (`client-session-static`, `contentscript-main-${tabId}`, the `livestore-devtools-iframe-` prefix, `/_livestore/browser-extension/`). Out-of-band distribution makes that a versioned contract, so it should become typed and shared.

3. **Which devtools suite relocates?** Two candidates with different blast radii: the **unit** protocol-compat test (3 cases, owned by `LS.SYS.VER.PROTO-R01`) or the **Playwright browser cell** (the `devtools` suite in the lane matrix). Relocating the browser cell partially invalidates `DELTA-003`'s close condition — it would be satisfied by removal rather than by fixing the policy gap.
4. **Where does a relocated suite live in contrib's intent layer?** Contrib has no verification branch and its rule is "one node per contrib package". Existing precedent/gap: `tests/sync-provider/` and `tests/integration/` already have no node.

## Verified state — 2026-07-29

Three independent read-only audit lanes reconciled every milestone against the tree rather than
against this issue's prose. Where they disagreed with the text, the text is corrected in place above
and below. **Percentages and counts in this section are measured, not estimated.**

### Where the work actually lives

The migration is **not** on `main` and **not** on the branch this issue's earlier sections were
written against. Canonical is:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Branch | `schickling-assistant/2026-07-29-devtools-migration` @ `81888e0` |
| Shape | 6-commit stack: effect-utils pin → core pin → `devtools-common` → release build hook → workspace/catalog → `devtools-react` |
| Published? | **No.** Unpushed, pending the sanitization gate below |
| Open PRs | #30 (effect-utils pin, draft, `BLOCKED`) · #33 (core pin, draft, `UNSTABLE`) |

An older worktree/branch (`schickling/2026-07-27-devtools`) is a superseded staging copy — **except**
for one regression, below.

### ⚠️ Regression: the Playwright toolchain was lost in the rebase

This issue states the Playwright toolchain "landed and independently verified". **It is not on the
canonical branch.** `rg 'playwright|nix-ld|LD_LIBRARY_PATH' devenv.nix devenv.yaml` returns no
toolchain hits at `81888e0`; the flake input and `devenvModules.default` import exist only on the
superseded branch. Only `tests/integration`'s `@playwright/test: 1.61.0` pin survived.

It cannot be cherry-picked as-is: the lost commit pinned the playwright flake at effect-utils
`b5e983b0`, and `mr:lock-sync-check` requires every Nix lock revision to match `megarepo.lock`, which
now records `165e63ee`. Re-landing it therefore forces the browser-revision bump this issue already
flagged — the cascade is unavoidable, not optional.

### Source migration: complete (2026-07-29)

**All four moving packages are imported**; `devtools-scripts` is correctly deleted (it *is* the artifact
producer). The earlier 114/174 figure is superseded.

**`devtools-chrome` (`20a6c50`) cleared its hard gate by replacement, not by escalation.** The private
`@overtone/utils/node` seam **never entered the public repo** — `pack-release` now derives `packageDir` from
`node:url` `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` with `CurrentWorkingDirectory.fromPath`, i.e. platform standard
library rather than vendored private code. Scans are clean for `@overtone`, `@overeng` and Generous across
the package and its VRS node. **So no relicensing decision was required.**

Two bonuses from that lane: it replaced a stale `@livestore/devtools-web-common/web-channel` import with the
public `@livestore/adapter-web/devtools-web-channel`, **removing a consumer of the #1510 orphan**; and it
proved `private: true` empirically rather than asserting it — a runtime replay of `simulate-publish`'s own
discovery predicate over real manifests returns `{total: 12, publishable: 11, chromeDiscovered: false}`,
exit 0. A browser extension demonstrably cannot reach npm through that path.

Still outstanding: 7 `devtools-react` support/doc omissions, **including all three Storybook config files**.

### Blocking on what is already landed

- **`devtools-react` cannot simulate-publish.** `@overeng/react-inspector` is a non-core `link:`
  dependency and `release/simulate-publish.mjs` rejects it. The vendoring step is unstarted, and it is
  larger than this issue assumed: **67 files with a three-package runtime closure** (`is-dom`,
  `is-object`, `is-window`), not "a copy of one package's `src/`".
- **Effect peer skew.** Both landed devtools packages declare `beta.99` peers while the workspace lock
  resolves `beta.98`.
- **Generated Tailwind drift.** `genie/external.ts:63` says `4.3.1`; the committed generated manifest
  says `4.1.18`. The generated surface is stale against its own source of truth.
- **The intent-layer check is falsely green.** All three `LSC.DT.*` ID rows are present, the three
  node directories are absent, and `bun tests/intent-layer/check.ts` reports zero violations. The
  suite does not verify that a declared namespace has a directory — a real gap in the checker, not
  just missing content.

### Independently confirmed

- **The Release/tag blocker is real.** Executable `gh release view|edit|create|upload` exists only at
  `scripts/src/commands/devtools-artifact.ts:614–640`; `release.ts` contains no relocation; no other
  git-tag writer exists in core's release machinery. Deleting the script still removes core's Release
  publisher *and* its only tag creator.
- **The `effect-playwright` diagnosis is correct** and unfixed: caller launch args are overwritten in
  extension mode.

### Corrections to counts used for sizing M5

`devenv.nix` is **679** lines (not 662), declares **seven** `release:devtools-artifact:*` tasks (not
four), and has **289** directly removable lines. `release/devtools-artifact.json` is referenced by
**eight** other files (not six). The artifacts spec section is **140** lines (not ~135); the runbook's
two named sections total **72** lines (not ~90), plus scattered references elsewhere. Core's devtools
suite relocation is **0 of 3** suites, not "1 of 3" — contrib's one `.play.ts` fixture is not one of
core's three.

`#1445` and `#1456` are **PRs, not issues**; `#1456` is already closed unmerged. `#1483` is **not yet
moot** — its trust boundary survives until M5 actually removes the bridge.

### ⛔ Publication gate: verdict is **DO NOT PUSH**

`livestore-contrib` is **public** and this source was private. A dedicated scan of the full
publication diff returned **DO NOT PUSH** on `81888e0`. Push was approved by the rights holder
*conditional on* this verdict, so the branch is held. No credential values were found; the blockers
are content, provenance and licensing.

| # | Blocker | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Captured fixture from a real session of an internal product: internal product-prefixed IDs, private sync-engine table labels, personal-domain OAuth redirect endpoints for three providers, production-shaped third-party media records | `devtools-react/src/utils/storybook/fixture-snapshots.ts`, ~30 sites |
| 2 | Private `@overeng/meters` specifier in copied-code JSDoc | `meters/debug-bag.ts:9` |
| 3 | Private internal project named in a TODO | `components/Meters.tsx:110` |
| 4 | Opaque shared ChatGPT conversation URL | `ShadowRootWrapper.tsx:87` |
| 5 | Opaque personal CleanShot share URL | `effect/background.ts:43` |
| 6 | Chromium-derived CSS names a BSD licence, but the package ships the LiveStore Community License and no BSD notice — the header points recipients at the wrong terms | `chrome-devtools-design.css:1-5` |
| 7 | The Community License's redistribution condition requires "the above copyright notice", and **no copyright notice exists in the file** — in both the package `LICENSE` and the byte-identical root copy | `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-LiveStore-Community-1.0` |
| 8 | **All six commit messages** carry internal agent-session-id, runtime-profile, skills-manifest and tooling-profile trailers (one duplicates the whole block) — requires a history rewrite, not a file edit | commit metadata |

**Withdrawn as a blocker:** `@overeng/react-inspector`. Verified public MIT in a public repo, with the
upstream 2017 Xiaoyi Chen notice and `UPSTREAM.md` provenance intact. It remains a **packaging**
defect — `npm view` returns 404, so the `link:` cannot resolve for any consumer — which is what the
vendoring work addresses.

### Private code copied into the public tree — rights-holder decision recorded

A file-level provenance scan found code copied or adapted from three internal packages that carry no
licence or NOTICE. **Decision (rights holder, 2026-07-29): relicense as first-party under the
LiveStore Community License, with provenance recorded.** Not removed, not reimplemented.

| Confidence | Files | Origin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| byte-identical | `meters/debug-bag.ts`, `engine.ts`, `grid/{FpsBlock,MeterGrid,PolyValueBlock,ValueBlock}.tsx`, `internal/utils.ts` | `@overeng/meters` |
| byte-identical | `utils/cn.ts`, `hooks/useStateRefWithReactiveInput.ts` | `@overtone/utils-frontend` |
| adapted | `meters/mod.ts` · `utils/download.ts` | `@overeng/meters` · `@overtone/utils-frontend` |
| structurally adapted | `JsonTreeViewer.tsx`, `JsonTreeViewerContextMenu.tsx` | `@overeng/bonsai-design` |
| related adaptation | `Table.tsx`, `Table.stories.tsx`, `theme/ThemeProvider.tsx`, `tailwind.config.cjs` | `@overeng/bonsai-design` |

**Owning the copyright does not license the leaked content.** Internal product names, sync-engine
labels and personal endpoints still have to come out regardless of the relicensing decision.

`@overtone/utils/node` does **not** appear in `81888e0` only because `devtools-chrome` and
`devtools-scripts` are absent — it will arrive with the Chrome import unless resolved there.

**A push becomes eligible only after** content remediation, the history rewrite, and a **fresh scan of
the final enlarged diff** — which will include the vendored inspector and the Chrome/Vite imports that
no scan has yet covered.

### Prerequisites now in review (core)

Both of M0's standalone core prerequisites are done and open as draft PRs:

| PR | What | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#1521](https://github.com/livestorejs/livestore/pull/1521) | GitHub Release + git tag creation relocated into `publish-release`, ordered after the npm publish; the `Release <version>` notes fallback dropped so a malformed plan fails loudly. Chrome ZIP upload left for M5 | `check-quick`, genie, lint, TS, focused 8/8, intent 8/8 green |
| [#1520](https://github.com/livestorejs/livestore/pull/1520) | `effect-playwright` now merges caller args with the required extension flags, with collected regression coverage | Targeted Vitest 1/1, `test:unit`, `ts:check`, lint green. **Browser proof advanced past "No devtools page found" and failed at the predicted published-v0.4.0 selector drift** — the diagnosis is confirmed by behaviour, not just by reading |

`#1489`'s attribution of that failure to the test is wrong and is corrected in #1520. The devtools
quarantine's stated reason is now **stale**; renew-or-remove ownership is still unassigned.

### Playwright toolchain: restored

Re-landed at `6b10294` on a working branch: flake/module and Linux `nix-ld` plumbing recovered,
repinned and relocked at effect-utils `165e63ee`, all contrib `@playwright/test` pins moved to
1.61.0, integration config + task + `pr/playwright` matrix added and the workflow/ruleset regenerated.
`mr:check` and `mr:lock-sync-check` pass; Chromium **1228** launches and reaches "Devtools connected".

The re-landed cell is **red for a real reason**: the connection transitions to *disconnected* during
the 35 s watch. That is a genuine defect the toolchain's absence had been hiding, not a plumbing
failure.

## Milestones

### M0 — Decide and record (blocks everything)

- [ ] **Relocate GitHub Release + tag creation out of `devtools-artifact.ts` into `release.ts` / the `publish-release` job.** Land this **standalone, ahead of and independent of this epic** — it needs no devtools work, reviews on its own, and is verifiable on the very next stable release. Relocate *within* the existing `publish-release` job so `gh release create`'s commitish resolution stays bit-identical and no new permissions are needed (`contents: write` + `GH_TOKEN` are already declared there). Order it strictly *after* the npm publish: a tag naming a version that never reached the registry is expensive to retract. Drop the "Release `<version>`" notes fallback while moving it — `release/release-notes.md` is committed by the release PR, so absence means a malformed plan, and that fallback is what caused the stale-body regression the source comments describe.
  **Invariant: core's tag + Release creation must be proven working from its new home through at least one real release before the script is de
limitations: Timeline, linked discussions, attachments and target code not acquired.

issues.title: Studio — an in-engine editing studio: maps, entities, logic, models, assets and Passion tools
issues.body:
> **Progress, 11 October 2026.** The first batch is merged (#74); the next is in review as #78. Of the 258 items below, **122 are finished, 118 are partly there** (each says how far) **and 18 are untouched**. A ticked box is finished and checked by driving the real interface; a **partly** note says how much of an item exists. What is built, how to use it and how it is validated: [`docs/studio-status.md`](https://github.com/marsninja/quakepassion/blob/main/docs/studio-status.md) (the branch's copy has what #78 adds).
>
> **Where each milestone stands:** 1 (shell) and 2 (blockout) are done. Most of 3 (views and texturing), 4 (brush power tools), 5 (logic and reuse) and 7 (curves and generators) is in. Parts of 6 (a light bake, a leak finder, cells that know what they see), 9 (the asset explorer, packing, previews), 10 (a model viewer) and 11 (terrain) are in. 8 (Passion tools) is blocked: expeditions do not load at present (#76). 12 (user walkers) is not started.
>
> **Checked on `main` after the merge** (565e24a, built locally): the fourteen scripted studio sessions pass, as do the menu check and the graphical checks for Quake, Quake II and three of four Quake III levels. q3dm1 fails its culling comparison in one small patch, which a build from before the studio also does (#77). The unit suites and walkthroughs were not rerun on `main`.
>
> **Open around it:** CI on `main` stops at the native build, because the pinned compiler lacks jac fixes the studio needs: jaseci-labs/jac#9935, #9942, #9971, #9973 and #9975 are merged upstream; #9978 (found in #78) is open. The pin needs moving to carry them. `scripts/stage_raylib.sh` leaves a library macOS refuses to load when it stages over an old one; the fix is on the next branch.
>
> **In #78 so far** (branch `feature/studio-next`): rings that turn and boxes that size about a pivot that can be moved, a group's own pivot, inflate, the texture lock; clicks that go through to what is behind, steps to the selection's owner, brushes and neighbours, brushes by number, named sets saved with the map, a tour of the selection and a swap; brushes stood on a picked face (extrude, cone, walls), faces taken off or turned round, side flags and detail, and diggers; two-, three- and four-view layouts, a ruler, zoom, names, remembered views listed, a backdrop picture and a camera that orbits.; groups with rows of their own in the scene list and their own visibility, lock, build and colour switches.; a played game held still and stepped by ticks, the selection played alone, build presets; the level shown as a skill or mode spawns it, a field-value replacer, a deeper logic audit, pasted gadgets with names of their own, and targets fired by hand during play.; several documents open at once with recent files, a right-click menu on the selection, face stepping, map-writing options and thin-face checks; duplicators that grow, turn about any axis, mirror on several, stand at named points and along paths, cycle materials and make entities of their own.; eight more shape builders, shapes that keep their numbers, caulk; terrain erosion, painting, rectangle lifts and triangle patterns.; patches that grow and shrink by a curve, thickness and fineness, an endcap; a slider, spinner, radio, vector field and colour bars in the toolkit and at the end of the inspector's forms.; materials wrapped round a corner, projected, fitted in whole repeats and painted by a drag, a face glued into a plane, a check for smeared materials.; keys bound by hand, a settings list, flat tones, grid numbers and a developer's readout.; handles for an entity's facing and a light's reach, paths drawn, a logic library and favourites.; a built level cut into cells that know which others they see.; the cells drawn, a bake kept and given back, recipes of build commands, other programs run over the map and their complaints gone to.; projects with a manifest and scenes of their own, add-ons of entity classes, and what each game's scenes begin with.; programs kept for kinds of file, image files read again when they change, and the mouse's options.; axis views held to a band of depth with the rest greyed or left out, and oblique views with a compass.; kept sets as layers, hidden and shown as one and saved with the map.; outlines swept along lines and paths, and swept again when the path moves.; a played game's firings counted, held on and its player and signals changed while held.; the start of the model editor: a model as a graph of parts and poses, primitives, mesh tools carried to every frame, MD3, MD2 and OBJ written; then picking by clicks, dragging points, tags and skins.; materials, classes and prefabs dragged from their tabs and dropped in a view.; faces linked to stay in one plane, carving that keeps divided faces linked, mitred seams and merged corners.; fine work on a terrain: corners moved with their kin, plots of cells outlined, lifted and painted, top and bottom moved apart.; entities that carry the game they are spawned by, and camp spots for bots.; Quake III shader scripts opened, changed by lines and stages, checked and saved.; sounds converted to what the games play, a wall texture's flags changed, animated textures' frames listed.; prefabs within prefabs, and instances that swap materials, set fields and take names of their own.; the model's skin: places laid, moved and turned on it, and its picture painted on the skin and through the model.; entities drawn in the 3D view as their game's models. **Next:** the smaller items still open in each section, and the larger pieces nothing has started: the rest of the bake (a partition by brush planes, bounced light, bot navigation), model and shader editing, user walkers.

## Usable when it ships

Press a key in `./qp` and the game you are playing becomes a document you can edit: fly through e1m1, click a door, change its speed in an inspector, drag a new room out of the void, wire a button to it by drawing an edge, press Play and walk through it — without leaving the process or running a compiler. Then open a Passion expedition and ask the generator to fill the room you just drew.

That is the goal: a Godot/Roblox-style studio living inside the engine, with the depth of a classic Quake toolchain. The feature inventory below is taken from [QuArK](https://quark.sourceforge.io/features.php) (the Quake Army Knife) and its [Infobase](https://quark.sourceforge.io/infobase/index.html), extended with the things QuArK never had: a live scene, play-in-editor, a visual logic graph, and a generator.

This reverses the current scope statement — the README and `docs/implementation-roadmap.md` both list an editor as out of scope. They get updated as part of this work.

## QuArK as inventory, not as implementation

QuArK is an offline tool: edit brushes, shell out to qbsp/vis/light, launch the game. Its features are the right checklist; its architecture is the wrong model. Three of its ideas are worth carrying over as design, not code:

- **Everything is a tree of objects with key/value "specifics"**, and game support is data, not code. That is a node graph.
- **Duplicators** are live generator objects, not copy commands: one original, the images follow. That is a node whose walker emits instances.
- **Explorer**: maps, models, textures, sounds and archives are all browsable items in one place.

QuArK is GPL and Delphi/Python; QuakePassion is MIT and Jac. Everything here is reimplemented from documented behaviour, the same way the engine reproduces the originals. No QuArK code or data files are ported.

## Decisions already made

| Question | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| UI toolkit | A Jac-native retained UI: widgets are nodes, layout/draw/hit-test are walkers. No raygui, no web panels. |
| Behaviour authoring | The Signal/Targets activation graph first (visual logic); hot-loaded user-written walkers as a later milestone, driven through jac upstream. |
| Geometry pipeline | Two tiers: instant live preview on every edit, plus a background bake (BSP, PVS, lightmaps). |
| Targets | Native QuakePassion projects; `.map` import/export; editing the shipped maps in place. Writing original-engine BSP29/38/46 files is **not** a goal. |
| Asset studio | Archive explorer and packer, model/animation viewer, model editing, texture and shader authoring. |
| Studio extras | Prefabs and an asset library, Passion generator tools, terrain sculpting. Live collaboration is out. |
| Packaging | A mode inside `./qp` (`QP_EDIT=1`, an `edit` console command, a key). Play-in-editor is a mode switch, not a process launch. |
| Tracking | This one epic; phase issues are split out as milestones start. |

## Architecture

```
editor/            new top-level package; depends on engine/, never the reverse
  ui/              the widget graph: panels, docking, tree, property grid, text, menus
  document/        Scene graph, project files, undo journal
  tools/           selection, transform, brush, face, patch, terrain ... one walker family each
  compile/         live preview builder and the bake (partition, vis, light, nav)
  formats/         .map reader/writer, archive and model writers
  assets/          explorer, texture browser, model editor
  passion/         generator stages exposed as tools
```

**The document is a graph.** `Scene` → `Group` → `Brush` / `Patch` / `EntityDef` / `Duplicator` / `Prefab` nodes joined by containment edges. Entity wiring is not a pair of strings to keep in sync: it is the same `Targets` and `Kills` edges the runtime already uses (`engine/world/signals.jac`), so the editor draws and edits the real activation graph. `targetname`/`target` strings are derived on export.

**Edits are walkers.** Every command is a walker spawned on the selection that records its inverse into an undo journal. Selection itself is edges (`Selected: Studio --> node`). Each command is registered in the existing console shell (`engine/console/shell.jac`, where commands are already nodes), so every editor action can be typed, bound to a key, aliased and scripted from a `.cfg`. That is the plug-in story.

**Live preview.** On each edit the affected brushes are turned straight into faces and collision planes (collision is already brush-based for Q2/Q3, `engine/formats/brush_collision.jac`). No hidden-face removal beyond brush-against-brush clipping, one visibility cluster, probe or flat lighting. The existence of `r_novis` suggests the renderer tolerates this; that is the first thing to prove.

**Bake.** A background pass produces what the shipped maps have: BSP partition, leaf portals, PVS, lightmaps, light grid, and bot navigation data. Passion already proves the path from an in-memory `Bsp` to a playable `Level` (`games/passion/generate.jac`, `geometry.jac`), but only for its watertight column grid — arbitrary brushes need a general compiler. Lighting reuses the pluggable `Occluder` in `engine/world/lighting.jac` and Passion's hash-keyed cache.

**Play-in-editor.** The document is snapshotted, the world graph is built from it exactly as a level load does, and Stop tears the world down and restores the document. Save/load already serialises the world, which is most of the snapshot.

**Entity classes are data generated from the engine.** The inspector's forms (fields, types, defaults, spawnflags, help) come from a declarative registry of the classes each game's spawn code implements — which the engine needs to grow — so the editor can never offer a field the runtime ignores.

- [ ] Groups: create, name, colour, nest, drag to reorganise *(QuArK New group, Change colors, Reorganize Tree)* — **partly:** create, name and colour (a `func_group`, picked, moved and duplicated as one); groups do not nest and nothing is dragged in the tree
- [x] Per-group visibility: visible, greyed, hidden, hidden in textured views only *(QuArK View Group submenu)*
- [x] Per-group "cannot select with the mouse" lock *(QuArK)*
- [x] Per-group "ignore when building" for partial play-tests *(QuArK Ignore to build maps)*
- [x] Layers / visgroups orthogonal to the hierarchy
- [ ] Prefabs: save a selection as a reusable item, organise in folders *(QuArK prefabs)* — **partly:** save by name and add a copy from the Library tab; one folder
- [ ] Templates: linked prefab instances with their own origin, scale and rotation; refresh from source; dissociate *(QuArK Templates, Refresh Template)* — **partly:** linked instances with their own origin, rebuilt from the file, and dissociate; no scale or rotation
- [x] Nested prefabs and per-instance overrides
- [ ] Asset library panel: prefabs, logic gadgets, materials, models and sounds from the project and the installed games, with thumbnails and search — **partly:** prefabs and saved scenes in a Library tab; materials in their own tab
- [ ] Import any `.map` into the current document as a group *(QuArK Import any map file)* — **partly:** `ed_import <file> [group]`; not yet in a scripted session

### 15. Terrain
- [x] Terrain grid builders in several triangle patterns *(QuArK Terrain Shape Builders)*
- [x] Raise, lower, smooth, flatten, noise and erode brushes with radius and falloff
- [ ] Basic selector: move every surface face inside a rectangle, with percentage and unit falloff *(QuArK Basic Selector)* — **partly:** every corner inside a rectangle lifted or lowered, with a falloff in units outside it, by command; no falloff by percentage and nothing dragged
- [x] Touch-up selector for fine work in 3D, with a variance setting for grouping common vertices *(QuArK Touch-up Selector)*
- [x] Move top faces, bottom faces or both *(QuArK Face Converters)*
- [x] Adjacent faces selector *(QuArK)*
- [ ] Texture applicator: paint materials onto terrain faces in 3D *(QuArK Texture Applicator)* — **partly:** a stroke of the brush gives the tops under it the material in hand, by command; face mode gives one picked face a material; no painting by dragging
- [x] Colour guide outlining grouped faces before an action *(QuArK Color Guide)*
- [x] Heightmap image import and export; convert imported terrain to editable form *(QuArK Import Converter)*
- [x] Compile terrain to brushes or to patches

### 16. Search, checks and diagnostics
- [ ] Basic checks before play: missing player start, bad targets, unknown classes, missing assets *(QuArK Basic checks)* — **partly:** player start, targets nothing is named, bad origins, brush entities without brushes, materials no archive holds
- [x] Find broken brushes and orphan faces *(QuArK Broken polys and faces)*
- [x] Find microbrushes and thin faces *(QuArK Find Microbrushes, Find Thin Faces)*
- [x] Find non-integral faces *(QuArK Find Non-integral Faces)*
- [x] Leak finder: flood from entities to the void, draw the leak line, step along it *(QuArK Holes in map, Load Leak file)*
- [ ] Portal display *(QuArK Load Portal file)* — **partly:** `ed_cells` draws a bake's cells in every view: the one looked from, those it sees and those it does not; there are no portals to draw
- [x] Problems panel listing every finding; click to select and zoom
- [x] Map statistics: brushes, faces, entities by class, lightmap area, texture memory
- [ ] Overdraw, PVS and frame-time overlays using the existing diagnostic overlay — **partly:** what a cell sees is drawn by `ed_cells`, and frame and build times are in the developer's readout; no overdraw view

### 17. Build, bake and play
- [ ] Live preview compile on every edit, incremental per brush — **partly:** the whole scene recompiles after every geometry edit
- [ ] Bake: CSG union, BSP partition, portals, PVS, area portals — **partly:** `ed_bake` cuts a built level's plan into cells that each know which others they can see, in the form the engine's generated levels use, so only those are drawn; no partition by the brushes' own planes, portals or area portals
- [ ] Bake: lightmaps, light grid / probes, light styles, coloured light, emissive surfaces — **partly:** lightmaps with coloured light, brush shadows and a minimum light, built with the level; no bounce, styles or grid
- [ ] Bake: bot navigation data for arena maps (bots route through AAS today, `engine/world/bot_routes.jac`)
- [x] Build presets: full, quick, fastest fullbright, selection only, rebuild without playing *(QuArK GO!, QuickGO!, Fastest, Complete rebuild)*
- [ ] Background baking with progress, cancel, and a content-hashed cache — **partly:** a bake's light and cells are kept under a mark of what was built and given back when the same thing is built again (an undo, a game played or stopped); baking is not in the background
- [ ] Light preview that updates as lights move, before any bake — **partly:** the level is lit again whenever a light is moved or changed
- [x] Customisable build menu; optional external compiler steps over exported `.map` *(QuArK Customize menu, Addons menu)*
- [x] Compile error navigation by entity and brush number *(QuArK Select Brush Number)*

### 18. Map formats and shipped maps
- [ ] `.map` read and write: classic Quake, Valve 220, Q3 brush primitives, Q3 `patchDef2` *(QuArK Supported Map Formats)* — **partly:** classic and Valve 220 read and written; Q3 `brushDef` (without its alignment) and `patchDef2` read
- [x] Options for integer-only coordinates and for comments in output *(QuArK Don't Write Floating Point Coordinates, Write comments)*
- [x] Open a shipped Q1/Q2/Q3 level in place for entity editing; save as an entity override the engine applies at load
- [x] Import Q2/Q3 BSP brushes as editable geometry (lossy texture alignment); Q1 BSP29 has no brushes and opens as reference geometry
- [ ] Open a Passion expedition as an editable document — **partly:** `ed_convert` is the same path as for Quake II and III levels, but expeditions do not load in the test environment, so it is unverified
- [x] Native project format: text, diff-friendly, one file per scene plus a project manifest

### 19. Asset explorer and archives
- [ ] One explorer over everything installed and everything in the project: maps, models, textures, shaders, sounds, cinematics, scripts *(QuArK Explorer)* — **partly:** everything installed, by game and folder; not the project's own files
- [ ] Browse PAK, PK3 and WAD contents as folders *(QuArK)* — **partly:** PAK and PK3 contents, by game; not WADs
- [ ] Preview any item: image, model, sound playback, CIN/RoQ playback, text — **partly:** images (WAL, TGA, JPEG, PCX), text, models as wireframes, and sounds (facts, and playback while that game's level is open)
- [ ] Extract files and folders; drag out of an archive into the project — **partly:** a file at a time, by a button or `ed_extract`
- [ ] Create and modify PAK and PK3 archives *(QuArK)* — **partly:** create from a folder (`ed_pack`); not modify in place
- [ ] Pack a project and only the assets it uses into a distributable archive *(QuArK Prepare used textures)* — **partly:** `ed_pack scene` packs the map with the Quake II and III texture files its materials name
- [ ] Dependency view: what a map uses, what uses an asset, what is missing — **partly:** `ed_stats` lists what a scene uses and the check names materials no archive holds
- [x] Import and convert sounds *(QuArK)*
- [ ] Asset search by name, type, game and tag — **partly:** by name, across every game

### 20. Texture browser, textures and shaders
- [ ] Texture browser with folders per game and per source, thumbnails, size filter *(QuArK Texture browser)* — **partly:** folders per game and source, thumbnails for all three games, a name filter
- [ ] Texture search *(QuArK Texture Search)* — **partly:** the materials filter
- [ ] Texture details: dimensions, flags, contents, animation frames, palette *(QuArK Texture details, Texture flags)* — **partly:** dimensions, in the face inspector and the explorer
- [ ] Texture lists and links to folders, so a project can reference rather than copy *(QuArK New texture list, Link to folder)* — **partly:** materials are names into the games' archives and the project's own folder; nothing is copied
- [ ] Import images as textures (PNG, JPG, TGA, BMP, PCX), with palette conversion for Q1 *(QuArK Texture Imports)* — **partly:** PNG, TGA and JPEG files in the project's textures folder are materials as they are; no conversion to a game's own format
- [ ] Edit texture sets: WAD (Q1), WAL (Q2) flags and contents; write them back — **partly:** `ed_wal` reads a Quake II texture's flags, contents, value and next frame and writes a changed copy among the project's textures; Quake's WAD files are not written
- [x] Open in an external image editor and reload on change *(QuArK External editors)*
- [ ] Used-in-level view and recently used — **partly:** used in the scene
- [ ] Q3 shader editor: stage list, blend functions, rgbGen/alphaGen, tcMod, animMap, deformVertexes, sky and fog parameters, with a live preview in the real renderer — **partly:** `ed_shader` opens a script (or takes the one the explorer shows), and sets, unsets, adds, drops and moves a shader's lines and stages by command, and saves it; no panel for it, and no live preview
- [ ] Shader script text editor with error reporting, side by side with the stage editor — **partly:** `ed_shader check` lists what the game would trip on, by line, in the Checks tab (braces, names, unknown or misplaced lines, words a line does not take, stages with no picture); the script is not edited as text in the studio
- [ ] Animated and warping texture preview (Q1 `+` and `*` names, Q2 animation chains) — **partly:** `ed_frames` lists a Quake `+` texture's row and a Quake II texture's chain; they are not played in the browser, and nothing warps
- [ ] Material slots for Passion districts editable as data

### 21. Model viewer and editor
- [ ] Open MDL, MD2 and MD3 models, sprites, and multi-part MD3 assemblies joined by tags *(QuArK Auto Assemble)* — **partly:** MDL, MD2 and MD3 open in the asset explorer; no sprites, and an MD3's parts are not joined
- [ ] Views: wireframe, solid, textured; multiple layouts; floating 3D views; rotation modes (free, lock to view centre, lock to model centre, rotate at start position) *(QuArK 3D Rotation Options)* — **partly:** one wireframe view that turns about the model and moves nearer
- [ ] Animation toolbar: play/pause, FPS, interpolation, smooth looping, interpolation frame count, play from `animation.cfg` *(QuArK Animation tool-palette)* — **partly:** play and stop at ten frames a second, and step a frame either way
- [ ] Frame list: select, rename, duplicate, delete, reorder; auto-rename matching frames across components *(QuArK Duplicate Current Frame, Auto Frame Renaming)* — **partly:** the frame's number and name are shown; in the model editor frames are copied, named, dropped and moved in the order, by command; they are not shown as a list
- [x] Components: multiple meshes per model; match frame counts; check components for errors *(QuArK Match Frame Count, Check Components)*
- [ ] Vertex, face and component selection; find by index; front-only / back-only face selection *(QuArK Find Vertices, Find Faces)* — **partly:** points and triangles picked by number, all, or by facing the view or away (`ed_pick`) or by a click in the view (Shift adds), and a part taken in hand; no find-by-index readout
- [ ] Move, rotate, scale, shift, mirror with axis locks and linear drag handles *(QuArK Movement tool-palette, X/Y/Z Axis lock)* — **partly:** `ed_mesh move|turn|scale|mirror` by numbers, an axis at a time, at one frame or all, and Ctrl and a drag moves the picked points in the view's plane; no handles drawn on the model
- [ ] Mesh tools: extrude, extrude with bulk, reverse face direction, subdivide 2/3/4, face cut *(QuArK Editing Tools tool-palette)* — **partly:** all but the face cut, carried to every frame alike
- [x] Primitive makers inside the model editor: sphere, cone, double cone, cylinder, dome, fan, torus *(QuArK Object modes)*
- [ ] Skin view: UV mesh editing, vertex and face selection synced both ways with the 3D views *(QuArK Skin-view page)* — **partly:** the picked points' places on the skin are moved, stretched, turned, flipped and laid flat by command (`ed_skin`), and the skin is shown with the part's triangles and what is picked in the 3D view over it; nothing is picked or dragged on the skin itself
- [ ] Skin management: several skins per component, import skin textures *(QuArK Importing Skin Textures)* — **partly:** a part's skins named, added and dropped and written with it; skins are not shown or imported
- [ ] Skin painting: solid colour, airbrush, pattern, colour picker, paint directly on the model or on the skin *(QuArK Paint Modes tool-palette)* — **partly:** a picture is made or opened, painted solid or as an airbrush on the skin or through the model by the pointer, and saved as a TGA; no patterns or picker, and the model is not drawn with it
- [ ] Tags: add, delete, drag, edit origin, per-frame matrices *(QuArK Tags System)* — **partly:** added, dropped and placed by numbers at one frame or all, kept through frame edits and written to MD3; not dragged, and their turning is not edited
- [ ] Bounding boxes per model and per frame; bounding box maker *(QuArK Bounding Boxes, Bbox Maker)* — **partly:** the model's box at the frame in hand is drawn and measured (`ed_model box`); no boxes kept as objects
- [ ] Bones: add, continue chains, assign and release vertices, per-bone colours, drag handles, key-frame spreading *(QuArK Bones System)*
- [ ] Vertex weights and vertex colours with a weights dialog and colour display *(QuArK Vertex Coloring and Weights)*
- [ ] Draw back faces, model axis, enlarged vertex ticks, handle drawing options *(QuArK Options menu)* — **partly:** the model's axes and ticks on the picked points
- [ ] Save MDL, MD2 and MD3; a native work format that keeps bones and editor state *(QuArK .qkl)* — **partly:** MD3 and MD2 written, and read back by the engine's own readers; no MDL and no work format
- [ ] Import and export interchange formats (OBJ and glTF first; ASE, LWO, MD5 if needed) *(QuArK Model Importers/Exporters)* — **partly:** OBJ in and out
- [ ] View-weapon and player-body preview using the engine's own rigs

### 22. Passion generator tools
- [ ] Open any seed as a document; regenerate with locked parts kept
- [ ] Mission graph editor: beats, links, tokens, cycle patterns, with the softlock proof run on every change
- [ ] Layout tool: place and resize rooms, re-route corridors, re-solve floor heights
- [ ] Recipe fill: pick a room and a recipe (hall, court, cavern, pit, arena ...) and generate its interior
- [ ] Director populate: fill a room or a route to a threat budget and roster; place resources along the intended route
- [ ] Playtester as a check: "is this map completable" on authored geometry, reporting the first unreachable objective
- [ ] Tension curve and niche descriptors shown as editable graphs
- [ ] District and material slot assignment per room
- [ ] Convert a generated region to plain brushes for hand editing — **partly:** the whole level by `ed_convert` (unverified, as above); not a region

### 23. User walkers (later milestone)
- [ ] Attach a Jac walker or node ability to a scene node as its behaviour
- [ ] Script editor panel with diagnostics from the jac compiler
- [ ] Compile and hot-load on save while the editor runs
- [ ] A sandboxed API surface: which nodes, edges and engine walkers user code may touch
- [ ] Custom entity classes defined in a project appear in the palette and inspector automatically — **partly:** as data: a project's add-on files of classes load with it and appear in the Classes tab and the inspector; not classes defined by walker code
- [ ] Project-defined editor commands and tools, loaded the same way — **partly:** a project's manifest keeps recipes (rows of editor commands under a name) that load with it; no commands written in Jac

### 24. Configuration and extensibility
- [ ] Editor settings as cvars, saved like the game's; settings panels for general, display, 3D view, map, model, files, colours *(QuArK Configuration)* — **partly:** the studio's settings are kept in `studio.cfg` between sessions and listed in one sheet, each line a click to change; they are commands, not cvars, and there are no panels by subject
- [ ] Rebindable editor keys through the existing binding system, separate from each game's bindings *(QuArK HotKeys)* — **partly:** any key, with Ctrl and Shift, bound to any editor command and kept apart from the games' bindings in the studio's own settings; only F8 goes through the engine's binding system
- [x] Mouse behaviour options per editor *(QuArK Mouse settings)*
- [ ] Per-game setup: asset directories, default textures, default build preset *(QuArK Games configuration)* — **partly:** `ed_game` keeps a material, a build preset and a bake for each game's scenes; the games' folders are still set outside the studio
- [ ] Game add-ons as data: extra entity classes, materials and prefabs loaded from a project or a shared file *(QuArK Add-ons)* — **partly:** entity classes from text files, shared or a project's own (`ed_addon`), and a project's own folders of textures and prefabs; an add-on file carries no materials or prefabs
- [x] External editor associations per file type *(QuArK External editors, File associations)*
- [x] List of loaded tools and add-ons; reload one without restarting *(QuArK List of Plug-ins, Reload)*
- [ ] Developer mode with memory and timing readouts *(QuArK Developer Mode, HeapStatus)* — **partly:** frame and build times and counts of brushes, entities and light samples in the status bar; no memory readout
- [x] Command-line entry: open a project, run a command script, exit *(QuArK command line)*

## Per-game notes

- **Quake**: BSP29 keeps no brushes, so shipped maps are entity-editable only. Textures need palette conversion and live in the BSP or a WAD. Lighting is monochrome lightmaps with light styles.
- **Quake II**: BSP38 keeps brushes and brush sides. Surface flags and contents are per face and matter to gameplay (ladders, currents, sky, warps). Units and hubs span several maps — a project needs a multi-scene notion.
- **Quake III**: patches, shaders, fog volumes, light grid. Arena maps need bot navigation data to be playable against bots.
- **Passion / native**: may mix all three games' assets and rules in one scene; this is the default project type.

## What the engine must grow

- A level built from brushes without a BSP tree, visibility or lightmaps (live tier), and rebuilt incrementally
- A general brush compiler: partition, portals, PVS, area portals
- A general lightmap and probe baker beyond Passion's column grid
- Bot navigation generation for authored arenas
- A declarative entity class registry per game, shared by spawn code and the inspector
- Entity override files applied at level load
- Mouse picking: rays against brushes, patches, models and entity boxes
- Several simultaneous cameras and render targets, orthographic projection, wireframe and solid passes
- Writers for PAK, PK3, WAD, WAL, MDL, MD2, MD3 alongside the existing readers
- World build and teardown that can be repeated in one process without leaks (play, stop, play)

## What this will ask of jac

The studio is the largest OSP surface the project has attempted: a UI as a graph, a document as a graph, tools as walkers. Expect compiler and runtime defects; each one is fixed upstream per the working agreement, not routed around. Known pressure points:

- Walker dispatch cost at UI scale (every frame, every widget)
- Graph mutation during traversal (edits while a walker is mid-flight)
- Graph snapshot and restore for undo and for play/stop
- Runtime loading of compiled Jac for user walkers — likely new upstream capability
- Native FFI for render targets and text input

Found so far, each from studio code:

| jac | What | State |
|---|---|---|
| jaseci-labs/jac#9935 | a C record that embeds a C record declared in another module | fix open |
| jaseci-labs/jac#9942 | a C record argument read from an optional slot | fix merged |
| jaseci-labs/jac#9971 | a container unpacked from `enumerate` or `zip` typed as a string | fix merged |
| jaseci-labs/jac#9973 | reversing or sorting a list of objects freed its elements | fix merged |
| jaseci-labs/jac#9969 | a local first assigned in a loop in an `impl` body taken for the archetype's member of that name | fix open (jaseci-labs/jac#9978) |
| jaseci-labs/jac#9972 | a loop target that rebinds a variable to another type goes unreported and corrupts memory natively | reported, open |
| jaseci-labs/jac#9975 | a dict literal keyed first by a string variable did not lower | fix merged |

## Milestones

Each is playable or usable on its own, and each gets its own issue when it starts.

1. **Shell**: edit mode in `./qp`, the minimum UI kit, fly camera, picking, entity inspector on shipped maps, entity overrides, play/stop. Proves the UI decision and needs no new geometry code. **Done** (#74).
2. **Blockout**: document graph, project format, `.map` import/export, brush primitives, transforms, undo, live preview, play from here. **Done** (#74).
3. **Texturing and views**: texture browser, face tools, multi-view layouts, scene tree, groups. **Mostly in** (#74): four views, grid, wireframe and lit display, the texture browser with pictures, face tools, and groups made and named; the tree does not show groups, and the other layouts and on-face handles are not there.
4. **Brush power tools**: CSG, clipper, vertex and edge editing, tag/glue/link, search and checks. **Mostly in** (#74): CSG, a drawn clip plane, corner and edge editing, tag and glue, search and the checks; linked and shared faces are not.
5. **Logic and reuse**: logic graph panel, prefabs, templates, asset library. **Mostly in** (#74): the logic graph with drag-to-link, copy and paste, prefabs (copied and linked), groups and a Library tab; live signals in play are not.
6. **Bake**: partition, PVS, lightmaps, leak finder, bot navigation. **Started** (#74): lightmaps with coloured light and brush shadows, and the leak finder; no bot navigation. In #78 a built level can be cut into cells with looked-up visibility; a partition by the brushes' own planes and portals are not there.
7. **Curves and generators**: patches, shape builders, duplicators. **Mostly in** (#74): patches as prism groups bent by their control points, shape builders, and duplicators as groups built with images; path, extruder and instance duplicators are not.
8. **Passion tools**: expeditions as documents, recipe fill, director populate, completability proof. Can be pulled earlier once Blockout lands. **Blocked** on #76: expeditions do not load.
9. **Asset studio**: explorer, archive packing, texture and shader authoring, model viewer. **Started** (#74): the explorer over PAK and PK3 contents with image, text, model and sound previews, extraction, packing a folder or a scene, and project images as materials; no shader or texture authoring.
10. **Model editor**. **Started** (#78): models open as wireframes with their frames (#74); in #78 a model is edited as a graph of parts and poses, made from primitives, reshaped by mesh tools carried to every frame, and saved as MD3, MD2 or OBJ. No picking by clicks, skin view, bones or tags editing yet.
11. **Terrain**. **Started** (#74): a grid of prisms sculpted by command or by dragging (raise, lower, smooth, flatten, noise), with heights in and out as images.
12. **User walkers**. **Not started**; needs compiled Jac loaded at run time, which jac does not offer yet.

## Validation

- Every editor command is a console command, so every feature gets a headless test: script the commands, assert on the document graph.
- Round-trip tests: `.map` → document → `.map`; project save → load; archive write → read with the existing readers; model write → read.
- Undo property test: any command sequence followed by the same number of undos restores an identical document.
- Live tier against bake: the same scene must collide identically in both.
- Baked authored maps run through the existing map sweep and walkthrough harnesses.
- Screenshot validation of the UI through `QP_CAPTURE`, as the rest of the engine does.

## Out of scope

- Writing BSP29/38/46 files for the original engines and other source ports (export `.map` and use external compilers instead)
- Live multi-user collaboration and anything else that needs networking
- Games beyond Quake, Quake II and Quake III (QuArK supports dozens; this does not)
- QuakeC editing or compiling — game rules here are Jac
- A marketplace or online publishing service

## Open questions

- Does the renderer and collision accept a single-cluster, tree-less level today, or does the live tier need a renderer path of its own?
- Where does the entity class registry live so that spawn code and inspector cannot drift?
- How much of Passion's playtester generalises from the column grid to arbitrary collision?
- What is the smallest upstream jac change that makes hot-loaded walkers possible in a native build?
- Project file format: a console-script style text file like saves and settings, or a dedicated graph serialisation?

issues.title: Design issue — parameter lattice v2: objective base units, integer canonical values
issues.body:
# Design issue — parameter lattice v2: objective base units, integer canonical values

**Supersedes:** the geometric parameter lattice of #239 ruling 5461507633-B, per owner direction
of 2026-08-30. **Sequenced AFTER #246 merges** (§9).

## Verification record

Designed by **Opus**; adversarially verified by **Fable**; errata folded; coordinator rulings baked
in as settled (§11).

| verification | result |
|---|---|
| blessed-site sweep (§4.3) | **21 M conversions bit-exact** against a correctly-rounded reference, including **disassembly-level confirmation of MXCSR immunity** — no FP-arithmetic opcode present |
| fixture sweep (§5.3) | **reproduced exactly**: 7 128 checked / 7 057 legal / 71 illegal, and the three findings F1/F2/F3 confirmed independently |
| rulings consistency (§7) | all **seven** rulings consistency-checked; A7 abridgement confirmed faithful, with two caveats now folded in as their own rows |
| errata | **5 confirmed and folded**: two ulp distances (114, and 114/1564), the F3 token provenance, four row counts in §1.2, and the SDK generator / README / `decimalToFloat32` dispositions |

Verdict: **SOUND**. Every erratum was a stated number that was wrong, not a conclusion that was
wrong; no finding, law, or disposition changed under verification.

**Status:** design + issue. No implementation, no worktree, no repo edits.
**Anchor:** engine `origin/main` @ `d6d6359edb5575c33d7e68b7c808359d37098f96` (fetched; all
file/line citations below are at that commit).
**Supersedes in part:** #242 as merged (`docs/derivations/242-parameter-lattice.md`), #239 ruling
A12, #242 S1's unit-class table.
**Lands after:** #246 (the app's vendored SDK is pinned there; see §9).

---

## 0. The redirection, in one paragraph

The owner ruled two sentences:

1. *"Maybe the step shouldn't be perceptual and should be unit-specific in an objective way
   instead. The perceptual layer could be built on the client side instead as an abstraction over
   the base step unit."*
2. *"Why don't we store parameter values in a numerical unit that doesn't have decimals?"*

Ratified interpretation, and the whole of this design: **every continuous parameter gets one
objective decimal resolution `10^-k` in its own native unit (the *base unit*), and its canonical
persisted value is an INTEGER count `n` of that base unit.** The lattice stops being a set of
generated geometric points and becomes the closed integer interval `[n_min, n_max]`. Documents
still spell human decimals; the decimal ↔ integer map is pure string arithmetic with zero
floating-point operations, which removes the rounding-mode hazard *by construction* rather than by
containment. `f32` is entered at exactly one integer→float site with a specified,
hardware-independent algorithm. Perceptual stepping — cents for frequency, ratios for time and Q —
moves out of the descriptor and into the SDK, where it computes a target and snaps to the integer
grid.

This is a strict simplification. It deletes `StepUnit::Cents`, `StepUnit::Ratio`, geometric point
generation, `MAXIMUM_LATTICE_POINTS` as a validation concern, the `f32` step word on the wire, and
the entire "does this row's rendering precision survive its own bound" class of defect. It costs
one new law (the f32-distinctness ceiling, §1) and one surviving exception (the Butterworth Q
default, §2.4).

---

## 1. Per-unit precision, with the f32-resolution argument

### 1.1 The law

> **L1 (distinctness).** For a row with base unit `10^-k` and declared value magnitudes bounded by
> `V = max(|min|, |max|, |default|)`, adjacent integer counts must map to distinct `f32`s
> everywhere in the row's range: `10^-k > ulp_f32(v)` for every `|v| <= V`.

`ulp_f32(v)` for `v` in the binade `[2^e, 2^(e+1))` is `2^(e-23)`. `ulp` is monotone in `|v|`, so
L1 reduces to a single test at the top of the range. Solving `2^(E-23) >= 10^-k` for the first
*unsafe* binade `E` gives a closed-form ceiling per `k`:

| `k` | base unit | first unsafe binade `E = ceil(23 + log2(10^-k))` | **distinct-safe while `\|v\| < 2^E`** |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1 | 23 | 8 388 608 |
| 1 | 0.1 | 20 | 1 048 576 |
| 2 | 0.01 | 17 | 131 072 |
| 3 | 0.001 | 14 | 16 384 |
| 4 | 0.0001 | 10 | 1 024 |
| 5 | 0.00001 | 7 | 128 |
| 6 | 1e-6 | 4 | 16 |
| 7 | 1e-7 | 0 | 1 |
| 8 | 1e-8 | -3 | 0.125 |

Worked check of the owner's own example, which is exactly right: at `k = 3` (0.001 Hz) the ceiling
is `2^14 = 16384 Hz`. At 8192 Hz `ulp = 2^(13-23) = 2^-10 = 0.0009765625`, so the margin has
already collapsed to `0.001 / 0.0009765625 = 1.024x` — one part in forty. At 16384 Hz
`ulp = 2^-9 = 0.001953125 > 0.001` and distinctness is **gone**: two adjacent 0.001 Hz counts are
the same `f32`. So "0.001 Hz fails above ~8 kHz" is the right practical statement and 16384 Hz is
the hard wall. At `k = 2` the ceiling is `2^17 = 131072 Hz`, which covers the 96 kHz launch rate's
Nyquist clamp (47998.867 Hz) with a **2.56x** margin and the 20 kHz EQ rows with **5.12x**.

### 1.2 The table

The owner's unit list maps onto the engine's `ParameterUnit` / builtin `BuiltinParameterMapping`
vocabulary as follows. `Q` and `%` and `pan` are not units in the enum; they are display faces of
`Ratio` and `Linear`.

| owner's unit | engine unit | `k` | base unit | worst shipped `\|v\|` | `ulp` there | `k_max` | margin | rows |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Hz | `ParameterUnit::Hz` | **2** | 0.01 Hz | 47998.867 (96 kHz clamp) | 3.906e-3 | 2 | 2.56x | `hpf_hz`, `lpf_hz`, 4x `band-N-frequency`, `crossover` |
| dB | `ParameterUnit::Db` | **4** | 0.0001 dB | 144 (`trim_db`/`fader_db` floor) | 1.526e-5 | 4 | 6.55x | 18 rows (+1 override) |
| dB (one override) | `ParameterUnit::Db` | **5** | 0.00001 dB | 24 (`ceiling` range) | 1.907e-6 | 5 | 5.24x | `miso.true-peak-limiter` `ceiling` only — see §5.4 |
| ms | `ParameterUnit::Milliseconds` | **3** | 1 µs | 5000 (compressor/multiband release) | 4.883e-4 | 3 | 2.05x | 15 rows |
| ratio / Q | `ParameterUnit::Ratio` | **4** | 0.0001 | 20 (compressor ratio) | 1.907e-6 | 5 | 52.4x | 12 rows (incl. the 4 `band-N-shelf-slope` rows) |
| % / pan / mix / matrix | `ParameterUnit::Linear` | **4** | 0.0001 | 1.0 | 1.192e-7 | 6 | 839x | 14 rows (9 effect + 5 builtin) |
| samples | `ParameterUnit::Samples` | **0** | 1 sample | 48000 | 3.906e-3 | 2 | 256x | `delay_samples` |
| choice / boolean | domain `Enumeration`/`Boolean` | **0** | 1 ordinal | — | — | — | — | 8 enum + 2 boolean rows |

Two rows are deliberately *not* at their `k_max`:

- **ratio/Q at 4 rather than 5.** `k = 5` is legal (52x -> 5.2x margin) but buys nothing: no
  authored value in the tree needs more than 2 fraction digits of ratio, and `k = 4` leaves a 52x
  cushion against a future row whose declared maximum grows.
- **linear at 4 rather than 6.** `k = 6` is legal, but 0.0001 already means 0.01 % on a normalized
  control, and it keeps the whole unit's rank span at 20 000 rather than 2 000 000.

**Verified against every shipped row.** All 78 continuous+builtin rows were checked against L1 and
against the span law below; the only two flags are the two known exceptions carried forward into
§2.4 and §5.4. Largest rank span in the whole catalog is **4 995 000** (compressor `release`, ms,
`k = 3`), which is `0.00116x` of `u32::MAX`.

> **L2 (span).** `n_max - n_min < u32::MAX` strictly. This is what keeps
> `miso_engine_builtins::DISABLED_LATTICE_INDEX = u32::MAX`
> (`crates/miso-engine-builtins/src/lib.rs:349`) permanently outside every lattice, which today is
> true only by accident of the geometric point counts.

### 1.3 What L1 is actually protecting

L1 is not aesthetic. Without it, two distinct canonical integers produce one `f32`, and then:

- the persist plane is injective but the *engine* is not, so a load→prepare→observe→save cycle can
  silently move a document if any surface ever reconstructs a value from the prepared word;
- a one-base-unit nudge produces no audible change, which makes the smallest rung of any client's
  ladder a no-op — the UX property the ladder exists to deliver.
