issues.title: fix: drop witness records whose source repository cannot be shown public
issues.body:
## What

Remove from crozier's current main the seven GitHub code-search witness records that the crozier history rewrite could not except. Each names one third-party repository that nothing shows was ever public: the GitHub API answers not found for it, its unauthenticated web page answers 404, and Software Heritage never archived it. Code search returning a repository is no proof it was public, and the user ruled that third-party content is purged from crozier, so these records go. The rewrite cannot drop them itself, because its rewritten main must keep origin main's tree. Once this lands, the prepared rewrite rebuilds history and drops the same records from every earlier commit.

Which records. The vault file crozier-history-rewrite/main-cleanup-needed.json lists them by path, line, record key and line sha256. It is under the exposure audit's private vault, the mode-0700 directory ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/ai-orchestrator/private-boundary-audit/ae88e3d8df238f0f/. The files are witness records under docs/openapi-surface/. Read that list only through small throwaway scripts in this dispatch's scratch directory. Those scripts print paths, line numbers and counts, never record text or the repository's name.

Where the list of what to remove lives. The exposure audit's private vault is a mode-0700 directory under ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/ai-orchestrator/private-boundary-audit/. Use the newest one holding terms.json, or the one the manager names if you ask. Its terms.json is a list of {text, class, rule, narrowed}; a term is referred to by its index in that list. findings-current-files.jsonl holds one {repository, path, location, term, class, narrowed, line, snippet} per hit in a repository's files as audited. The vault is private and is the only complete list. Nothing public may carry its contents: no task text, title, commit message, branch name, change-request title or description, committed file or report names a term, quotes a snippet or states a per-term count. So read the vault through small throwaway scripts kept outside the checkout (in this dispatch's scratch directory). Have them print this repository's own paths, line numbers and term indexes, never term text or snippets, and keep term text out of your messages, so that nothing downstream that reads this dispatch's transcript can repeat it. Judged false positives go to the vault's exceptions file, `exceptions.jsonl` in the same directory: mode 0600, append-only, one JSON object per line, {"repository": "<owner>/<name>", "term_index": <int>, "reason": "<why it is not a private reference here>", "node": "<this node's id>"}. Create it if absent. Other cleanup nodes append to it concurrently, so append whole lines and never rewrite it. An exception is never recorded in the public tree. A term terms.json marks `narrowed` is an exception the audit already recorded. It is checked only in its narrowed form: a generic-word name or package only inside its private owner/name, and an owner shared with public repositories not at all. Never record such a term again. Every text this change publishes, including the commits, the branch, and the change request's title and description, describes the work generically, for example "replace third-party-derived fixtures with synthetic ones". It names no term, path quote or count from the audit. The re-audit of the landed repository against GitHub is the manager's, after landing, and is not this node's bar.

Remove each listed record as a whole. Where a check, census, test fixture or document counts those records or depends on one being there, update it so it still does its job. Use a synthetic record in the same schema where a check needs a record to exist. Change no source behaviour.

## Why

The user ruled that crozier's history is purged of third-party content, and that the rewrite's proof excepts a match only where its context shows it reveals nothing private. These records fail that test, and the history push stays held until they are gone from main.

## Acceptance criteria

- None of the records main-cleanup-needed.json lists remains anywhere in the branch's committed tree, as a whole record or with only its matched words changed. No file in the tree (contents or paths) names the third-party repository those records named. Both are checked locally against the branch by a scratch script that prints only counts.
- Every check, census, test fixture or document that counted or depended on a removed record still does its job against the tree as delivered. Each test and witness-backed check over the touched files is driven through crozier's real interface, the CLI or public entry point it already exercised, and passes. The deterministic lint over the touched files and the repository's judged lint over the finished diff are green.
- Nothing this dispatch publishes carries private audit material. The branch's committed tree (file contents and paths), the messages of the commits this branch adds, the change request description the worker leaves and the dispatch's report contain no match of any term terms.json lists under that term's `rule`. A term terms.json marks `narrowed` is checked only in its narrowed form. A term is excepted only where exceptions.jsonl records it for `nickderobertis/crozier` with a reason that truly states why each match it excepts, read in its own context, reveals nothing about a private repository. None of them quotes a vault snippet, states a per-term count, pairs a term index with a path or line, or names, paraphrases or describes the removed records' repository in any wording.
- Every claim the dispatch's report makes about the delivered work and its verification is true of the tree as finally delivered.

## Additional info

No history rewrite, force-push, or edit or deletion of any issue, change request, board item or commit is authorized; this node changes only the current tree on its own branch. Operational checks owed: the tests over the files this change touches, the deterministic lint over them, and the judged lint over the finished diff. No publication term check does this node's work for it, so the vault guidance above and this task's criteria are the whole guard: hold every text this change publishes (files, paths, commit messages, the branch name, and the change request's title and description) to the vault's terms yourself, and remember that paraphrase is invisible to any term list.

## Additional info

### Operational notes for this host

**Run only the checks that exercise what you changed.** The tests that cover the code
you touched, the lint that reads your diff — and nothing wider. The repository's own
automation runs the full bar downstream on the change this work becomes: a `pre-push`
hook where that repository publishes locally, the host's required checks where it
publishes remotely. Neither is waiting for you to have run it first, so running it here
spends twenty to forty minutes of this dispatch learning what the merge path reports
anyway. That is measured rather than estimated: one node in this workstream spent about
84 minutes on three rounds of everything its repository could run, to reach lint findings
a diff-scoped run reports in two.

**Pick those checks from your change, and take the narrowest scope each one supports.**
One test module over the whole suite; the lint over your diff over the lint over the
tree. A repository's own fast deterministic tier is a fine choice when it is what
exercises your change — its `just --list` says which recipe that is — and a poor one when
you reached for it because it was the widest thing available. When a check you ran
reports something, fix that and run **that check** again; nothing here asks you to re-run
its neighbours to confirm, and a wider tier cannot re-check a finding it never made.

**A dispatch that changed nothing tracked owes none of them.** When your deliverable is a
document, a report, or an answer, there is no changed code for those checks to exercise
and you are complete without them — decide that from what the repository shows, never
because running them is slow or inconvenient. `git status` reporting nothing to commit is
then a correct and complete outcome, not a problem to solve by writing a file nobody
asked for.

**A publication check runs downstream, so no worker can run it and none is judged on it.**
The host's required checks and a repository's `pre-push` gate run on the change this
work becomes, after this dispatch settles: downstream publication checks are not
runnable by a worker, and a dispatch is never held to one having passed. That holds on a
retry too. A `checks-failed` retry — a re-dispatch onto the same branch carrying the
merge path's refusal and `onevcs`'s evidence — is judged on its task's stated local
acceptance checks: the repair of what the refusal named, proven by the checks the task
names, and never by the downstream check passing again, which can only happen once the
retry has settled. One retry that fixed and locally verified the failing test its
refusal named was failed for not re-running the required check, which left finished
work unpublished and its dependents skipped until a manager published it by hand.

**Never signal a process you did not identify by PID, and a PID you got from a pattern is
still a pattern kill.** Several managers share this host, and their dispatches, drivers,
publications and test servers run under the same few binary names — `just`, `node`,
`python`, `onepipeline-api` — so a kill by name knows nothing about *whose* work it
matched. The distinction is the tool rather than the pattern: `pgrep` and `ps` **read**,
and either spelling of them is fine, `pgrep -x` included; `pkill` **signals**, and it is
never the answer here, in any spelling. `-x` is the trap, because it reads as the careful
one — `pkill -f 'just gate'` at least needs a narrowing pattern, while `pkill -x just`
takes every `just` on the machine. Reading the table first and piping the pids into `kill`
is no way around it: that is the same pattern kill with more steps.

Two workers reached that place from different directions on 2026-08-24, while another
manager's dispatch had been live over an hour. One ran `pkill -TERM -x just`. The other
ran `ps -eo pid,args | grep 'onepipeline-api serve' | awk '{print $1}' | while read pid;
do kill "$pid"; done` — which obeys the letter of every paragraph below and does the same
damage, because `just dag-ui` and the e2e suites both spawn that server and a pytest run's
were alive at that moment.

**The one process you may signal is one you started yourself, so capture its PID as you
start it:**

    cmd & MYPID=$!
    kill "$MYPID"

Anything you did not start belongs to somebody. Read what it is, report what you found,
and leave it running.

**A wait written against a full command line never ends, because one of those command
lines is yours.** That is a different defect from the one above — it wedges your own
dispatch rather than somebody else's — and it is why `pgrep -f` cannot be waited on.
`pgrep -f` matches its pattern against every process's whole argv and excludes exactly one
process — itself — never the shell that invoked it. So any pattern naming the thing you are
waiting for is, by construction, a substring of the command line of the shell doing the
waiting: `until ! pgrep -f "just gate"` matches its own loop and never exits, and so does
the same loop written against `llmlint-judge.sh`, `scripts/fetch-corpus.sh`, or
`publish-branch`. That is a defect in the polling mechanism rather than a fact about gates,
so it applies to every wait you write.

That has wedged four workers here, and then two more workers and the manager itself in one
night: seven instances of one defect. A crozier corpus audit waited in `until ! pgrep -f
'scripts/fetch-corpus.sh'` with no fetch running at all — the only two matches were its own
polling shell and the manager's diagnostic shell — and waited until it was interrupted. A
`check-plan-bar-conflict` dispatch waited on `! pgrep -f "llmlint-judge.sh"`, whose negation
could never become true, and was cancelled and killed; its replacement then reached for
`pkill -f` against three patterns, which is not a wait at all but the same self-match with a
signal attached, and is refused above. And the manager, an hour after instructing a worker
about this, guarded a launch with `pgrep -f "publish-branch" && echo ABORT || launch`, whose
pattern was a literal substring of the launching shell's own command line: it aborted
unconditionally and then reported a publish as RUNNING that did not exist. That last one is
the evidence that matters most — a rule its own author reproduces an hour after issuing it
is a rule whose wording is the problem rather than its reader.

**Wait with a sentinel file.** Background the whole command you are waiting on — one
command, so that what you waited on is what you meant to run — and poll for a file only
that invocation can write:

    ( just test > /tmp/check.$$.log 2>&1; echo $? > /tmp/check.$$.exit ) &
    until [ -f /tmp/check.$$.exit ]; do sleep 20; done

**A process must finish inside the turn that started it.** Backgrounding is how you wait
on a slow command *within* one turn, which is why the launch and the wait sit together in
that example — both halves belong to the same turn. What does not survive is a background
process left running when the turn ends: nothing carries it across, and the launch gives
you no sign of that, because it succeeded and the turn then ended normally. The loss
shows up a turn later as a sentinel that never appeared and a recipe terminated by
signal, with the whole run to pay for again. It bites hardest where it is most tempting,
because a worker reaches for backgrounding exactly when a command is slow enough to
threaten the turn — here the judged lint tier and a whole test tier, which are the two
runs a node most needs to have made. So run a slow check in the foreground, or background
it and wait out its sentinel before your turn ends; never end a turn intending to read a
result on the next one.

**To ask whether a process is running at all, match the executable, not the command line.**
`pgrep -x onepipeline` matches process *names* exactly — the binary, not its arguments — so
the shell doing the asking, whose own name is `bash`, cannot match it however the pattern
is spelled. Where the binary name is not distinctive enough to identify what you mean
(`just`, `node` and `python` run everything), read the process table instead and drop the
one self-match that form has:

    ps -eo pid,args | grep -v grep | grep 'lint-llm-diff'

Both of those are **reads**, which is what makes `-x` safe here and forbidden the moment
the tool signals. The replacement for the worker wedged above reached for `pkill -f "just
gate"`, `pkill -f "just check"` and `pkill -f "nx run"` while another manager's run was
live. Read to learn what is running, report what you found, and signal nothing you did not
start.

**One sentinel and one log per invocation, and look before you launch one.** That pair is a
shape rather than two literal paths. Several dispatches run on this host at once and they
share `/tmp`, so a second worker writing `/tmp/check.log` writes into the first one's — and
`until [ -f /tmp/check.exit ]` returns immediately on somebody else's exit file, reporting
their result as yours. Name both after the invocation (`/tmp/check.$$.log`, or the node
id), and, before starting it, check whether its sentinel path is already in use by another
invocation; if so, choose a different invocation-specific pair. This path-ownership check
does not prohibit concurrent checks or judged tiers. Three workers collided on shared names
today and not one of the three failures read as what it was: two
deterministic-tier runs deadlocked against the same cargo target-directory lock, so both
logs sat unchanged and neither progressed — about fifteen minutes lost and three
interruptions to a live turn; two whole-e2e runs wrote to one log, and stopping the
duplicate left four `SIGTERM` entries in it that read exactly like real test failures; two
judged-tier runs raced and wasted a roll, which was harmless only by luck. Read a log that
has stopped growing as two commands blocking each other before you read it as one command
working.

<!-- llmlint: ignore[contracts_have_one_source_or_a_drift_gate] The source of this contract is the engine that exports the variable, and it lands in the same run as this paragraph: there is no released copy to reconcile against yet, and this task is explicitly told not to go looking for one in an installed engine. `tests/test_dispatch_appendix.py` holds these four properties and no more, so the day the engine side is adopted the drift gate has an exact set to reconcile. -->
**Write the files this dispatch needs under `ONEPIPELINE_NODE_SCRATCH_DIR`, rather than
under a `/tmp` path you invented.** It is an absolute path to a directory that exists and
is writable when the dispatch starts, is unique to this dispatch, and is not removed while
it runs.

**Root-owned files after a container run.** The pre-push visual guard captures in Docker
as root and can leave `.nx/` and `dist/` unwritable, failing the *next* check with `NX
Permission denied (os error 13)`. There is no passwordless sudo; repair from inside a
container:

    docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/w -w /w mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble \
      chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /w

**If a test fails in a way that makes no sense, check the host before the test.** On
2026-08-19 two publication attempts against the same already-green branch failed on two
unrelated tests — a 5-second timeout, then a browser remote that never came up — and both
were written up as flakes. The host was at 197G/197G, and the next attempt said so
outright with `No space left on device`. A full disk does not announce itself to a test
runner; it announces itself as an unrelated test failing. One command rules it out:

    df -h /home .

**If a rule looks wrong or misapplied, say so with evidence rather than editing it.**

**One suppression policy, and this is the whole of it.** A site-scoped `ignore` directive
is permitted where the rule is genuinely misapplied at that site **and** the directive
carries a substantive reason saying why. What is forbidden is silencing a finding you
have not answered so that a count moves. What you owe an account of is **every
suppression your own diff writes — added, moved or rewritten — and every one already
standing over a line that diff changes** — each with its site and its reason, in your
completion report, so the manager reads what you left rather than discovering it. Both
halves are decided from the diff alone: a directive line inside it, or a changed line
inside the region a directive covers. A file-scoped directive is outside both unless your
diff writes the directive itself — its region is every line of the file, so counting it
would make this file's own header a debt of every change that edits a word of it.
Suppressions elsewhere in the tree are not yours to inventory: this repository carries several hundred standing directives, and
a list of them would be longer than the report is read under while saying nothing about
the change under review.

That scope is stated because the sentence it replaces read two ways at once: its first
clause reached every directive anywhere in the repository, while its second — *so the
manager reads what you left* — was about this dispatch's own work, in the same breath. A
node was failed on the wider reading for not accounting for suppressions it had never
touched, on a tree whose every target had just run from cold and come back green; it cost
a third dispatch of a run's final node. The reading above is the one the purpose clause
and the scale both support, and it is written so that a worker complying with it and a
judge reading it adversarially land in the same place. It says which lines rather than which sites for the same
reason: *site* was itself readable two ways, and the first worker to apply the sentence
could not decide whether the file-scoped directives at the head of `AGENTS.md` were
owed by a change that edits one of its paragraphs. Apply that same test to whatever
replaces it: read it as a worker trying to comply and as a judge looking for a way to
refuse, and if the two can land in different places it is not one source yet.

`AGENTS.md` states no suppression policy of its own and points here, because this file is
what your judge reads beside your task: while that document said it twice, one
dispatch added four site-scoped ignores each carrying a substantive reason and was failed
for *"the task's categorical instruction never to suppress a rule"* — work that was
correct under one of this repository's own readings and refused under the other.

**`--no-verify` is not an acceptable response to a slow or inconvenient hook.** The hooks
are this repository's enforcement point — there is no CI — so bypassing one commits work
that nothing has checked, and nothing you run afterwards catches it: a check runs over
the finished tree, by which point a bypassed commit is simply history. Two workers
today reached for `git commit --no-verify`, both on a commit they had judged mechanical,
and one of the two was a *merge* commit — a conflict resolution, which is the single most
likely commit in a dispatch to be wrong. No check caught either one; the monitor caught
both. If a hook is slow, wait for it. If it refuses, it is telling you something about the
commit in front of you, and the answer is to fix the commit.

**Commit a coherent working piece the moment it works.** A dirty worktree does not
survive this dispatch: what is uncommitted when your last turn ends is what nothing
recovers — not a retry, not a recovery verb, not a manager reading the branch. So each
piece is its own commit as you finish it, rather than one commit held back to the end.
*The moment it works* is the moment you have seen it work: the checks that piece needs
are run before it is committed rather than after, so that each commit is one you have
evidence for.

**Ask rather than stop.** When you cannot proceed without a decision that is not yours —
a frozen contract you would have to amend, a goal that reads two ways, a constraint you
would have to relax — put the question to your manager over `$ORCHESTRATOR_ASK_MANAGER`,
which every dispatch carries, and go on working on whatever does not depend on the answer.
Ending your turns with the work undone and the question unasked is the one response
nothing can recover: a worker that reasoned about a frozen contract correctly, declined to
amend it unilaterally, named two options for its owner, and then stopped for three turns
lost about fifteen minutes of correct work and settled reporting `ahead of main: 0
commit(s)`.

**Draft a follow-up that can wait; never draft one that cannot.** Work you notice that
is outside your subtask — a bug beside the code you touched, a missing test or script, a
stale document, an improvement to this harness or to the context agents are given — is a
follow-up, and doing it is not yours. Record each one the moment you notice it by piping
its body into `"$ORCHESTRATOR_FOLLOW_UP_DRAFT"`, whose `--help` names the flags and the four
headings that body carries; the command stamps where it came from. Do not collect them into
a list at the end of your last message instead, because nothing reads that list. A draft is
unverified — a follow-up agent checks every one after the run — and it is not your
completion report, which still says what you did. Drafting is only for what can wait:
anything blocking, whether a decision fork, a constraint you cannot meet, or something your
manager should act on now, goes over `$ORCHESTRATOR_ASK_MANAGER` immediately, as the
paragraph above says, and is never drafted in its place.

**A GitHub rate-limit refusal that `gh api rate_limit` disagrees with is the secondary
limiter.** The primary limit is the one that endpoint reports and the one a wait answers.
The secondary limiter is reported by nothing, polled by nothing, and not waited out by
polling — every further attempt extends it. So when a `gh` call is refused for a rate
limit while `gh api rate_limit` still shows budget, stop making that call: deliver the
result another way, name in your report what was refused and what you tried, and leave the
retry to a person.

**Publication goes through the harness.** The session branch reaches its remote only
through `onevcs publish "$ONEVCS_SESSION"`, and its change request is lifted, landed or
kept for the user's review by the lifecycle after you settle. No `git push` of the session branch, no `gh pr create`
for it, no `gh pr ready`, no `gh pr merge`. Finish the branch, commit everything, leave
the tree clean, and report. Landing it is explicitly **not** yours to perform and **not**
part of your acceptance criteria. Two things are yours, and each only when this task's
own `## Additional info` — its own words above these notes — says so:

- **Only when the task's `## Additional info` says the change request may be published
  early**: `onevcs publish "$ONEVCS_SESSION" --draft [--title T] [--body-file PATH]` opens
  the session's change request as a draft, and a later `publish --draft` pushes new
  commits onto that same change request and never opens a second. Commit everything
  first — a dirty tree is committed for you, under a provenance you did not choose.
  `onevcs change describe "$ONEVCS_SESSION" --body-file PATH` replaces its description
  and `onevcs change show "$ONEVCS_SESSION"` reads it back. The description you leave is
  what the drafter finishes from, so start it with what only you know — the evidence and
  where it is. Never mark the draft ready yourself; after you finish, the lifecycle lifts
  it or keeps it as a draft for the user's review according to the repository's policy.
  `ONEVCS_SESSION` is in every lifecycle dispatch's environment.
- **Only when the task's `## Additional info` authorizes a throwaway demonstration change
  request**: after the draft is open, cut a branch from the session branch, commit the
  demonstration on it, push it with `git push -u origin <branch>`, open it with
  `gh pr create --draft --base <session branch> --head <branch> --title "DO NOT MERGE: …"`,
  capture the evidence — `gh pr view <n> --comments`, `gh pr checks <n>`, and `gh api`
  **reads** of that change request's own comments, checks and reviews, never a write to
  anything — then close it with `gh pr close <n> --delete-branch`, return to the session
  branch, and delete the local branch — a local branch left behind makes the session's
  close refuse. Its base is always the session branch, never the repository's base; it
  is never marked ready; it is closed before you finish.

Everything else a push or a change-request verb could do is still not yours.

**A branch you resume may already be on its remote, and a published branch only grows.**
A retry — a `checks-failed` one among them — re-dispatches onto the same branch, which an
earlier publication may already have pushed. So check before you touch its history: `git
fetch` and `git log origin/<branch>`, or the published commit your task's context names.
The repair of a branch already on its remote is new commits on top of the remote's
commit — never an amend, a rebase, a squash, a reset or a force-push of commits already
there. One retry that fixed both refusals its merge path named by amending the two commits
already pushed was refused `non-fast-forward` when it published, and settled
`push-rejected` with the correct tree stranded on the host.

**Every claim you make about the finished work is true of the tree as it finally
stands.** That is the property you are held to, and it says nothing about where your
report sits. This conversation does not end when you report — your supervisor keeps
asking, and answering well means running things — so a report required to be this
dispatch's literal final output is one no correct worker can give. What is required
instead is that nothing you have said about the work is untrue of the tree by the time you
stop.

When work follows your report, say in that same turn what changed and what you re-ran. A
correct delta satisfies this exactly as fully as restating the whole report does. Silence
does not satisfy it at all. Your last substantive turn should leave a reader able to say
what the finished tree contains and what was verified about it, whether that comes from
one report or from a report plus the deltas after it.

**A claim about a check, a test, a lint run, or a commit that was not run or was not made
is false, and fails on its merits.** A report asserting a check passed on a commit where
no such run occurred is that case, and one node of this host's history was correctly
failed for it. So do not carry a claim forward across a change that could have invalidated
it — re-run what the change could have broken, or say which claims you have not re-checked.

**Evidence deliberately about an earlier or induced state is not a false claim.** Proving
that an assertion can fail means making it fail, reading the message, and reverting;
proving that a message used to say nothing means quoting the run from before the change.
A citation of a run taken before a change, or of a failure induced on purpose as evidence,
is correct evidence — provided the citation says which it is. One node of this host was
failed for exactly that: its own criteria required its assertions be observed failing, and
the resulting-tree property above was read as forbidding the citation that requirement
produces.

**A commit that cannot affect a check leaves that check's evidence standing.** *Could have
invalidated it* is a condition, and a commit that fails it does not reach the claim — so a
run taken before a later commit is still evidence for the tree after it, provided the
report names that commit and says why it is inert for that check. What decides it is what
the check reads, never what kind of change the commit is. A comment-only or
documentation-only commit to content a check does not read is inert for that check; the
same comment is not inert for a check that reads comments, which a judged lint does, so
that one is re-run or named as not re-checked. A commit touching anything a check reads is
not inert for it, however small. Two dispatches of one node, about 45 minutes each, were
refused over nothing but a comment-only final commit after their cited check runs, with no
change in whether either tree was correct, and the manager had to send *re-run after every
commit* three separate times to get past it: read as absolute, the conditional rule above
is one no worker can meet, because every commit comes after the last run.

The ordering demand this replaces — that the report come after everything else, and that
anything found later be repaired and the whole report written again — is **withdrawn**. It
failed six of fourteen nodes in one workstream, each with complete committed work, a green
deterministic tier, and no acceptance criterion found unmet, and two of those carried an
escalated warning about it in their own task and failed anyway. A bar finished work
cannot clear teaches everyone to route around the thing that enforces quality; the
property above is what that demand was serving, and it is what survives.

### State the bar in `## Acceptance criteria`, not only here

A judge reads this node's `## Acceptance criteria` and its own review bar. Where the
criteria are silent about something the bar demands, it imports the demand and applies its
own reading of it — and finished, gate-green work has been failed twice that way: once for
running the gate's parts separately, and once for never having *"provided a final verified
completion report"*, a demand in neither the task nor the shared completion clause.

So every demand this node will be held to is stated as a criterion of its own, including
the two the bar makes of every implementation dispatch:

- the behavior this node adds is **proven end to end** by a test or journey that drives the
  real interface, rather than by inspection;
- every claim the dispatch makes about the finished work — what it verified, and the
  evidence for it — is **true of the tree as it finally stands**.

Criteria state properties of the finished tree; the commands that produce them belong in
this section. Whether the criteria answer every demand their own bar — or this appendix —
makes of them is read by `just review-plan <source:project>`, which spends a judged turn
on it and judges it by meaning: criteria that state a demand in their own words answer it,
and no criterion is refused for failing to use a particular phrase. Nothing reads it
deterministically any more, because the phrase matching that did refused wordings the same
review had just asked for.

issues.title: Map the Proseweaving plugin and review-writing policy landing
issues.body:
## Destination

Land Proseweaving's tested human-facing writing procedures and adversarial draft pass, Mergecraft's review-voice composition and reviewing-others-prs successor, and the selected evaluation-evidence requirements. Complete the accepted medium-aware writing correction and its separately owned, reproducible Hatchery adoption. Preserve applicable portable macOS source and GitHub-hosted CI assurance without requiring another remote-host deployment.

## Notes

### Coordination

**Orchestrate Proseweaving through completion** coordinates this execution map; **Orchestrate Provingkit preview rollout** confirms that it retains whole-Kit allocation and continuing source-compositor allocation, with no accepted successor; **Codex Foreman** retains cross-harness delivery. Existing source and adoption owners retain their work; archiving a chat or opening a new context does not transfer ownership. Foreman reports actual release acknowledgment from the existing Claude source lead; the release-delivery gap is closed. Preview retains continuing source-compositor allocation, with no accepted successor or duplicate allocation. The [2026-10-08 coordination snapshot](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/12#issuecomment-6061285374) retains historical instructions and bindings. Later human decisions govern. Refresh claims, source, routes, and windows before dispatch; human joins need Ivan's answer.

For Ivan’s current October 11 OOM recovery, Foreman’s acknowledged current policy permits 20 ordinary workers across cooperating lanes and serializes each shared capacity and pending-memory reservation. Current MemAvailable already includes running workloads; subtract the current shared pending-launch budget once and require 32 GiB remaining. Use 4 GiB provisionally for an unmeasured ordinary worker, and retain that pending allowance until its actual start receipt. Consume the latest ledger before each reserved start; old capacity snapshots are superseded. This review group keeps one active reviewer at a time. Check current memory availability, swap use, and memory pressure before new starts against Foreman’s current thresholds; hold expansion on unexpected pressure or a newly observed OOM. Recover existing children/results before replacing an unrecoverable unfinished worker. Preserve completed work without replay. This group runs the remaining critic scopes and adjudication sequentially; keep required experimental concurrency intact under its own admission. Lightweight recovery, bounded reads, writing, and authorized publication continue independently. This temporary recovery rule changes no source, evidence, approval, or acceptance contract. Agree shared source/regeneration/evidence/review/host windows; second landers rebase/revalidate. Preserve originals/private evidence/unrelated members/frozen inputs/acyclic graph. Use `wayfinder`, `delegating-cross-agent-work`, `handoff`, child checklists, standing capture/Git/PR/check contracts, and reviewed downstream invocation. Observe routes; accept latest harness unless specified otherwise.

[Match writing to its medium and adopt Proseweaving locally](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/106) and its four decision children are closed. The accepted division remains: Proseweaving supplies generic prose/conditional conversation, global instructions personal voice, Mergecraft PR/review voice, Tricritical structural output. **Refine PR body voice guidance** retains the adoption and durable-recreation notes. Canonical source/`CONTEXT.md` govern; Task Witness stays optional.

### Parallel preparation and joins

- **Constructing pragmatic agent policies** owns [Land Praxis’s shell with constructing-agent-policies](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/209), then [Encode, evaluate, and land the seed policies in Mergecraft](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/210). The native snapshot shows that all blockers of the Praxis shell are closed. **Constructing pragmatic agent policies** remains the source lead through Foreman; no replacement allocation is accepted. Foreman’s newer retained public source-lead return reports a clean local, unpublished repair commit `b02632a` on `9d6667a`. The next double check is admitted and its relay is posted, but actual lead receipt/start and a clean double-check result remain unconfirmed. Completed measured harness steps were each below 1 GiB; those measurements do not establish review acceptance. No landed shell/seed handoff is verified. The lead’s next step is that double check, then both acceptance halves under the selected Real-run bar and the applicable review/publication steps, respecting Foreman’s memory admission. This owner-reported progress supplies no landed shell/seed handoff. Foreman reports an actual continuation acknowledgment from the existing source lead after Ivan’s release; the release-delivery gap is closed. The expanded private source/capability handback remains with Foreman’s prepared approval boundary after automatic disclosure review rejected it. Continuation acknowledgment does not establish source acceptance or a landed shell/seed handoff. No landed shell/seed handoff or clean combined source result is established. Preserve existing worktrees, held-out domains, reservations, independent approvals, and completed work. The next skill-text author must have seen neither held-out domain.
- **Diagnose Mergecraft PR publication failure** is archived. Preview confirms that its handoff covers the isolated runner, while continuing source-compositor allocation remains with Preview after the merged-source/procedure/inventory handoff. **Diagnose auto-mode classifier denials in Provingkit flows** retains [Honor one merge-closeout push answer in Versionkeeping](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/425) after build handoff, outside alpha.4: investigation reported, no implementation. Coordinate seed wording and second landing; consent stays branch/remote-specific.
- **Orchestrate Provingkit preview rollout** owns [Teach writing-for-people to decompress operator briefs](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/27) and its separate adapter-validity correction. Its retained pre-restoration private candidate is `db497be1cbe4ab9aee4480ddc6b2ab5ee871905278e6228e4e97ef6bd42102b5`; the later corrected candidate is recorded below. Preview consumed the independent withdrawal disposition and corrected the demonstrated defect through the approved reservation/process-completion interface. The earlier incomplete packet intake and Runtime return containing a shortened read remain uncredited. Its usable replacement Runtime report identified a P2 concern: a stop signal during prior-handler restoration could leave affirmative eligibility or completion. The independent adjudicator accepted that source finding after complete report and required-source intake; actual usability was recorded in the original live binder. Requery claims and coordinate shared source and host windows before dependent execution. <!-- proseweaving-unseen-handoff-dispatch:20261007 -->

Ivan selected an extension of the existing `resolving-workflow-ownership` procedure for [the decision-premise correction](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/449). **Orchestrate Proseweaving through completion** prepared an isolated four-file dotfiles source checkpoint at local, unpublished `c5f211321a06ab02e1222cd835e99837a8b8b034`: a narrow description and paragraph correction, twelve synthetic application cases, six description-selection cases, and their separate answer key and comparison method. All 236 owning tests passed on the unchanged committed files. The supplied-context comparison returned correct application decisions in all three arms. The baseline missed three desired description triggers; the corrected and simpler arms selected all six cases as expected, using byte-identical descriptions. This one batch establishes neither superiority of the longer paragraph nor product-native discovery or general benefit. Original comparison dispatch records retain the unsupported desktop profile spelling and have joined the shared desktop allocation through Preview and Foreman; their raw outputs remain documentary input, not an accepted dispatch binding. No accepted desktop producer exists yet, and #463 closure alone is not a prerequisite or a remedy. A bounded request to use desktop native subagents for this ordinary source-review loop awaits Ivan’s answer; it preserves the unknown desktop version and does not qualify the maintained helper or another consumer. Independent corrective-decision and evidence review, the maintained-source owner's adoption decision, authorized publication and installation, and supported downstream invocation remain separate acceptance claims. The writing correction proceeds independently; a claim to correct the whole external-help incident still needs both corrections exercised on the same final scenario. <!-- proseweaving-premise-source:20261008 -->

### Final source, review, and evaluation joins

The retained local composition is `5d807c45b01ae4d2d97a0a7ee700843ed196c5be` on parent `cdfdef5`, with focused source checks, scoped reviews, and verified source/handoff inventories. It is an immutable prepared candidate, not today’s main or final qualification. Preserve it and its packet while the PR84 owner creates a separate persistent successor worktree from the post-Praxis, post-seed-policy merged revision.

That owner combines the retained writer/editor source and Mergecraft successor, including [meaningful workflow names and grounded questions](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/pull/365) and [the finished-draft editor](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/pull/127). Preserve PR365’s six added cases and evidence; verify compatibility across the combined lineage. Close those two PRs as superseded only when the combined source lands, as [Ivan decided](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/256#issuecomment-5957001472). Keep the three original historical evaluation files byte-identical and outside provider-delivered inputs.

The [source-frontier refresh](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/19#issuecomment-5961436903) found no independent source edit left for review voice or the PR-description register. After the policy handoff, recompute their overlaps and agree the PR-description file window with [the repository-ownership contribution](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/195). Reconcile shared canonical source, regenerate affected projections, content locks, and the Kit definition, and renew affected review and evidence on the combined revision. Respect the shared relation-evidence reservation; the second lander rebases, regenerates, and revalidates rather than copying a stale identity.

Join the prepared inputs with that candidate by verifying the delivered source and applicable behavioral method. Obtain a finite supported harness, grader, and discovery allocation before providers run. The retained source-lane plan freezes the evaluator and repairs harness isolation and reviewer-record gaps before diagnostic regrading, the unchanged-text baseline, and decision-dependent incident evaluation. The owner confirms their current status and adapts the plan to the actual answers; fresh source-lane runs wait for the applicable preparation checks and that allocation; the separate Receipt-refresh hold still applies. The full corpus requires three applications per case under the selected method, preserving stricter retained criteria. Earlier panel approvals and description-routing probes do not qualify this source.

Qualify Proseweaving jointly with [Mergecraft review voice](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/19) and [the PR-description register](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/111) against one selected catalog. Include actual review-voice calls to the writer, fallback behavior, and affected discovery. The existing review-voice owner retains its execution and integration. Review-voice completion also requires complete selected consumer evidence, final source review, and landing verification after the seed policies. Only then hand qualified review voice to [the reviewing-others-prs successor](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/20), after a live graph check. Adding that skill changes the catalog: renew affected native discovery under a separately reviewed finite allocation. Reuse application evidence only where its delivered inputs and method permit, preserving every original observation’s binding. A single final run is not promised.

The [retained corpus and origin contribution](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/blob/333afc7db07815002b771cc63e1c795a04b5d298/evals/proseweaving/usable-references/README.md) contains 26 writer and 12 editor cases. The reviewed intermediate constructor/packet contains three repetitions, 114 prospective application jobs, and 36 separate query packets for one prospective candidate condition. Independent construction, original-source correspondence, packaging review, and coordinator byte intake passed. This proves preparation, not allocated execution, an ordinary Receipt, an accepted multi-condition comparison matrix, behavioral qualification, or installed acceptance.

The reviewed disposable Codex observation exposes both entrypoints as standalone repository skills. The separate Claude Code 2.1.287 observation accepts the native adapter manifest non-strictly and attributes one enabled Proseweaving session plugin to the supplied source slice. These are metadata observations; they do not establish skill or companion ingestion, namespaced invocation, model behavior, or adoption. Further loading and behavior observations need the reviewed final candidate and their own finite allocation. Accept and migrate to the latest available harness version unless Ivan specifies otherwise.

Preserve the [landed Receipt reconciliation](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/pull/383), PR391’s earlier publication audit, recovered historical evaluation originals, prior source checks, failures, and client observations under their original bindings. Mergecraft’s retained Markdown run used older Proseweaving instructions. None of those records, a closed ticket, a static check, or an installation record supplies current behavioral or runtime evidence for the final candidate.

### Adoption, reconstruction, and retirement

The selected route is ad hoc installation of Proseweaving, Versionkeeping, and Mergecraft. Its final reviewed source/artifact pins and live acceptance do not wait for full preview, alpha.5, formal Base Loadout, or full alpha.3 publication. The separately reviewed maintained marketplace selection is empty; that is a different route, not a cancellation of the three-member selection.

Reobserve the Codex marketplace baseline before choosing a transition. Different-source rebinding with affected registered members unselected is unavailable through the maintained route; selected-only updates at its owned stable source remain supported. Preserve the three-member selection and return a concrete mechanism or scope decision only if that observed condition applies. Coordinate one actual shared registration, cache, configuration, and instruction-write window with the host-rollout and preview owners. Report changed installed identities, preserve frozen preview inputs and unrelated members, and require fresh loading and invocation acceptance, durable reconstruction, and separate Cursor-client acceptance before the relevant removal.

The [durable-producer clarification](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/300#issuecomment-5958908519) retains [Restore the review-before-you-ship policy as standing user-level rules](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/389) with **Restore review-before-ship rules (dotfiles#389)**. That producer owns its Claude-rule and matching Codex-template spans; preserve its decisions and coordinate through the foremen. Its [standing-policy source](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/pull/408) is merged, but acceptance remains open. **Refine PR body voice guidance** returned a read-only closeout proposal: the complete Claude target matches; the shared Codex review section matches and occurs once; the entire Codex difference is the accepted local removal of the obsolete `systematic-debugging` caller. I verified both target postimages and the immutable policy/test bindings. The owner observed configured status and a complete in-memory render comparison; I did not replay them. No review-policy apply is needed. Whole Codex synchronization waits for [the canonical troubleshooting-source correction](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/pull/417) to land and a fresh complete comparison. The existing accepting owner remains unchanged and unavailable through its current route. A named accepting-owner choice, current target acceptance, reconciliation of the real reviewed-change record, and the ticket’s settled stopping conditions remain before closeout. Do not repeat a completed review merely to invent a retrospective policy-load record. The runner’s final review input now records loading the merged shared procedure; I verified its input identity, and the adoption owner retained it separately. This is owner-reported consumption, with no observed runtime-load trace or accepted clean consumer review while desktop binding remains unresolved. No completed review or acceptance proposal was replayed. The twelve port-first removals wait on this acceptance and their other named ports. All four retirement-eligible sources still require verified replacement and durable reconstruction; eligibility permits no early removal.

**Refine PR body voice guidance** owns the current caller-retirement work under [the durable recreation producer](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/300). Its [honing-caller repair](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/pull/416) is public at `6a50dc5af7e17da783c7e8553919716475b62d97`; the owner reports clean source review, passing source checks and disposable installation/recovery preflight, and completed CodeRabbit and Greptile approval, captured in [its review handoff](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/300#issuecomment-6047388017). Merge and installation wait for [the Linux portability check transition](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/pull/412), owned by **Orchestrate CI on Codex**. The CI owner now reports the successor receipt signed and canonically published at body sequence 5 on unchanged `2f67bd9638bb6f2b4383fa0bd33998f66529ffea` over `3feb1c44317338dcc8b63fce38d6db58f592abba`, with exact readback and [trusted-base admission success](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/actions/runs/37739284111). Its portability results and CodeRabbit approval remain on that commit. PR412 has not landed. CI reports its required checks and reviews pass and has presented the prepared operation to resolve the fixed-timestamp conversation and squash-merge the reviewed commit. That separate merge decision awaits Ivan’s answer in the CI chat. Main-based synchronization waits for actual landing. This is separate from Provingkit Receipt-retention design acceptance. The PR join adds no native map dependency and establishes no installed adoption. After landing, the retirement owner carries the reviewed two-skill installation, affected-client discovery, and real honing invocation on [the missing-required-equipment procedure](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/414), coordinated with **Orchestrate Provingkit preview rollout**. Preview reports [the troubleshooting instruction correction](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/413) locally deployed and consumed; [its source PR](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/pull/417) remains draft and unmerged. The [required-equipment repair draft](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/pull/418) is published above it at unchanged `dc82e3e4c2e189396f7000a9478c346046bb4309`. Preview consumed the final clean source review and the completed ordinary CLI text loop in its original coordinator; the earlier incomplete leader and first revised adjudicator’s input-location failure remain preserved. The current body discloses the lower PR’s wait for the CI correction to land on `main`. I matched both public draft identities and complete title/body digests and read Preview’s final verification. The lower PR’s original canonical evidence remains preserved; its new navigation publication is sequence 3. Upper text and evidence are unchanged. The original aggregate Graphite repair remains incomplete. **Codify repo configuration guidance** completed the investigation of [the audit-argument correction](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/487) and [unchanged-member evidence preservation](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/488). Preview has a concrete correction proposal; method choices and new test boundaries remain unconfirmed before dispatch. Investigation and isolated proposals can run concurrently; coordinate their shared source, tests, and instructions. The argv fix can land separately; preservation consumes it for combined verification, [targeted installed adoption](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/139), and authorized resume of the original immutable handoff/checkpoint. Verify every member before aggregate closeout; preserve confirmed completions and refuse drift or weaker evidence. Original handoff and receipts remain intact; the new lower body differs from the original target. Resume must refuse that drift unless a separately bound successor handles it. Preview reports successful native Stack creation through GitHub’s UI, with exactly the two PRs over `main`. Preview completed the three critics and separate adjudication with no findings, then published the lower PR’s reviewed body-only navigation and verified its canonical audit and native Stack rendering. The finite publication is complete; earlier inputs and failures remain preserved. Source and canonical draft publication establish no behavioral qualification, receiving acceptance, or adoption. A retained handback alone supplies no authenticated execution evidence to another leader; the ordinary CLI review supplies no authority for the separate desktop exception. I returned a frozen [required-equipment action-method proposal](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/414), matching 35 source files to the clean published candidate. It proposes disposable local operation controls and a separate observer; offline replay alone cannot qualify agent behavior or native receiving acceptance. No implementation worker is assigned. The evaluation directory and README reservation remain proposed; Preview will consume it and obtain Ivan’s tdd seam confirmation before dispatch. Behavioral/discovery observations, source landing, installation, actual invocation, and receiving acceptance remain. Preserve the existing instruction and review-slot reservations. The Pinewood offline transport/supervisor preparation continues independently. Each source landing, installation, real invocation, durable recreation, and retirement retains its own acceptance evidence. <!-- proseweaving-adoption-ci-join:20261007 -->

Ivan separately authorized September 18 local deletion of `reviewing-before-finalizing`, `pr-review-orchestration`, and `reviewing-others-prs` in the originating installation task. That bounded action remains separate from successor qualification and other retirement gates. The [wrapper behavior trace](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/6#issuecomment-5736199865) feeds the existing source-disposition comparison, review-voice producer, and reviewer successor with their native prerequisites intact. Global instructions retain personal voice, authorship, operating policy, and necessary invocation pointers; verified replacements absorb portable mechanics.

### Standing contracts and closure

The accepted [medium-aware writing and adoption contracts](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/106) remain settled. Proseweaving owns generic human-facing prose mechanics; `writing-for-people` is its portable entrypoint, conversational guidance is conditional, and personal voice composes through consumer-global instructions. Mergecraft owns PR-description content and review-specific voice; Tricritical owns structural review output. Cross-plugin composition calls `proseweaving:writing-for-people`; projections remain intra-plugin. The adversarial skill’s reviewed preparation still needs final qualification and landing.

Use current `CONTEXT.md` and source in `nisavid/provingkit`; the port and rename have landed. The current Kit contains Rolecasting, Tricritical, Versionkeeping, Mergecraft, Artifact Customs, and Proseweaving. Task Witness is optional future equipment outside the current Slate. Historical decisions below retain the terms and scope recorded at the time. Model-specific research remains evidence rather than portable policy.

This map carries implementation, review, publication, and acceptance through completion. Keep one local orchestrator; use `wayfinder`, `delegating-cross-agent-work`, and `handoff` at substantial boundaries. Fresh contexts do not transfer an active owner’s responsibility, and HITL choices require the operator’s actual answer. Read authoritative child instructions and checklists before work. Check reservations before shared source, topology, validators, policy, projections, README, locks, or host writes.

Use `capturing-agent-procedures` for maintained procedures and downstream invocation. Bind consumers to reviewed producer revisions, supported inputs, and completion evidence; keep the native graph acyclic. Keep private host, account, configuration, and recovery evidence outside public tracker text. For Git use `checkpointing-and-publishing-git-work`; for PRs use `publishing-reviewable-prs` and `writing-reviewable-pr-descriptions`. Run `git diff --check`, owning validators/tests, and the disposition check where required. Follow each member README’s regeneration commands: Proseweaving’s lock writer also projects its roster; Mergecraft’s Markdown projection and lock writers are separate. Reclassify each concrete dispatch and review with current `choosing-agent-models` guidance.

Apply the [personal-repository platform-assurance scope](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/258#platform-assurance). Hatchery is the only live target. Applicable macOS source and GitHub-hosted CI contracts remain; runner-inaccessible behavior is explicitly unqualified and nonblocking. The prior work-Mac apply below is historical evidence.

Finish the native implementation children and Receipt-retention execution map, then verify the separately owned three-member Hatchery adoption against its durable dotfiles producer. Keep that adoption ticket in this map’s native children with its existing source and installer prerequisites. The completed medium/adoption and artifact-planning maps stay closed. Whole-Kit preview, historical relation repair, Base Loadout publication, broad shared-skill convergence, and unrelated deployment maps remain independent. Disposition remaining fog against delivered behavior before closing this epic; do not silently count it as implemented or expand the current increment.

The [accepted alpha publication contract](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/296#issuecomment-5897710926) has its finite lane under [the preview map](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/66). Consume relevant publication handoffs without importing whole-map completion into targeted adoption. [Uniform plugin artifacts for a later 0.1 alpha](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/405) and the broader historical-blob integrity guarantee remain unselected later fog, outside current preview/alpha.5 completion; neither adds a Receipt-design or Proseweaving completion gate.

## Decisions so far

- [Rename the writing plugin to Proseweaving](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/pull/47): merged as `3df83efee027a39f79cb113aaa21954ae2d4c723`; the portable entrypoint is `proseweaving:writing-for-people`, with a thin Claude-native `proseweaver` adapter. Earlier names and identities below describe historical evidence.
- [Match writing to its medium and adopt Proseweaving locally](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/106): planning is complete; the accepted [writing contract](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/109#issuecomment-5724287968) and [installation contract](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/110#issuecomment-5724551512) govern the priority source and adoption chain. <!-- decision:106 -->

- [Reconcile the review-writing skill cluster against dotfiles f700471](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/13): adopt the Comment Voice section and two post-baseline writer behaviors; the rest of the cluster is superseded by canonical coordinators, with `44ee979` already covering the same-day `getting-prs-merged` edits.
- [Land the review-writing cluster reconciliation](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/14): merged as `4dc20b4` (PR nisavid/agents#96); writer contract and merge coordinator adopt the three carried behaviors, and the ledger records the `reviewing-others-prs` supersede-and-remove fate at contribution level plus the Tidesmith-facing writing-style rationale.
- [Bootstrap the Tidesmith plugin](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/15): merged as `5a3c829` (PR nisavid/agents#97); package skeleton, generated registry, validator with validate-then-publish lock writer, and 21 tests, kept out of marketplace and release identity pending the slate decision.
- [Implement Tidesmith's generic writing skill with evals](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/16): merged as `d292aa9` (PR nisavid/agents#98); `writing-for-people` publishes the portable register, evidence discipline, and usage-judged edit pass with seven evals; the validator enforces the per-skill eval contract and requires PyYAML.
- [Port the generic writing clauses into the global Writing section](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/22): merged as `fbf2047` (PR nisavid/dotfiles#254); the global Writing section carries the grounding, evidence-guard, edit-pass, register, batch-variance, and brief-decompression clauses as whole-sentence pins, the em-dash rule is judged per usage, and the runtime-outcome guard is scoped so source-established behavior stays a plain declarative (scoping carried to Tidesmith via the split ticket).
- [Decide Tidesmith's Provingkit slate membership](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/21): Tidesmith joins the first release slate; the Kit is seven plugins, the port (#25) carries the membership mechanics, nothing reviewed reopens, and the repository glossary (#30) owns the terms.
- [Backport the review-voice improvements into the dotfiles review skills](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/23): merged as `a10ae79` (PR nisavid/dotfiles#256); `reviewing-others-prs` carries the ask ladder, comment evidence shape, load-bearing credit, and pre-post batch edit pass, defers shared clauses to the global section, and gains five behavior evals and a `review-output` test case.
- [Pull and apply dotfiles on the work macOS host](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/24): applied under the standing two-way sync rule; the host runs dotfiles `main` `a10ae79` with the Writing section and the review skill live; the three Hindsight templates stay for their own branches.
- [Decide the Mergecraft→Tidesmith dependency declaration](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/18): a route, declared as `external_calls: ["tidesmith:writing-for-people"]` in Mergecraft's topology and resolved by its validator with an owners check; reduced-claim degradation stated once in the review-voice reference; nothing in the manifest beyond a README sentence.
- [Codify eval receipts as a PR readiness and merge gate](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/29): a committed per-skill receipt bound to content-lock, eval, and fixture digests gates ready and merge through `validate_<plugin>.py --source-stage` and the Mergecraft coordinators; CI checks the receipt and never executes evals; thresholds live in `release/behavior-eval-policy.json`; waivers are operator-only; implementation is #33 and #34, disclosure is #28.
- [Initialize Provingkit's agent docs and glossary with setup-matt-pocock-skills](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/30): merged as `64060b3` (PR #31); `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/`, and a `CONTEXT.md` glossary that leads with Agent Plugins v1.0.0 terms and notes Claude Code's equivalents second; the `main` ruleset needed a temporary, restored amendment and now also allows squash merges.
- [Split writing-for-people by concern](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/26#issuecomment-5733420642): the medium-aware source landed at `91af898ef72fce984a4843071e9fbf33cf878113`; the receipt-only successor reconciled its retained evidence after landing. <!-- decision:26 -->

## Not yet specified

- Documentation-authoring migration into Proseweaving: rescout `applying-diataxis` and `honing-human-facing-docs` against the [public Diátaxis documentation design](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/211) before proposing ownership or scope.
- Whether audience-grounding or stopping-point reports need another portable skill after the current writing split and operator-brief treatment; whether `writing-for-agents` belongs in this plugin despite its different audience. Do not turn unsettled placement into installed policy.

## Out of scope

- Blanket resync of unrelated shared and unledgered dotfiles skills, owned by [Converge source skills](https://github.com/nisavid/agents/issues/51).
- Retirement of the maintained dotfiles `reviewing-others-prs` source or its durable declarations, and removal of independent equipment without demonstrated replacement coverage. The separately authorized September 18 local wrapper deletion is outside this map and does not wait for successor adoption.
- Full-preview or signed whole-Kit release qualification, replacement of frozen preview inputs, remote-host deployment, and historical PR-body repair. The independently owned three-member ad hoc adoption does not wait for these.
- A formal comparative matrix beyond the applicable [Provingkit release contract](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/3), or changes to the seven-field source-shape contract owned by [the portable GitHub Markdown implementation](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/9).

The PR-specific imperative-summary and subject-centered-opening correction is merged in [PR #543](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/pull/543) at `c1858b8621205032e3b68e73ed3e87ea34a8cd2c`. I verified that all six landed files match the reviewed candidate. The required checks and canonical publication audit passed; CodeRabbit withdrew its tracking finding and approved. The [publication-register task](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/111) retains its partial contribution ledger and remains open for composition and behavioral qualification.

The shared source window is released for the existing reviewer and composition work on current main. Preserve the native completion joins from [Praxis's shell](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/209) through [Mergecraft's seed policies](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/210), [review-voice integration](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/19), and the publication-register task. Independent preparation can continue through its existing owners; shared source and generated identities still need coordinated integration and renewed affected evidence.

The [targeted host installation](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/112) and [durable chezmoi recreation](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/300) retain their qualified-source, selected-artifact, fresh-session, reconstruction, and item-specific retirement joins. The installer's one pending qualification question remains with its existing owner. The [shared interim signer](https://github.com/nisavid/dotfiles/issues/369) remains an independent prerequisite for [preserved alpha.3 publication](https://github.com/nisavid/provingkit/issues/297).

The refreshed native map has 25 children: 13 closed and 12 open. Its five unblocked open children are already claimed; there is no unclaimed frontier requiring another dispatch. This source landing does not complete the publication-register task, qualify the full feedback-response procedure, or establish a live installation or retirement.

issues.body:
Tracking issue for running the [0.0.8 milestone](https://github.com/rickylabs/netscript/milestone/25) as one orchestrated run. The run is launched by a `/swarm` comment on this issue, and its coordinator reports back here.

The plan below was copied from the owner's reconciled plan, last updated 2026-10-07. It is a **proposal**: Step 0 must still ratify scope and get an independent PLAN-EVAL before any implementation is dispatched. Live state on GitHub (milestone membership, issue state, merged PRs) overrides this text wherever they disagree.

## Complete 0.0.8 Groups

C2-C6 mean proposed **0.0.8-canary.2 through .6**. These are planning allocations, not published labels.

**Breaking changes and migration notes**
- **#2193: service CORS is explicit.** There is no wildcard default any more. Set `NETSCRIPT_CORS_ORIGINS='https://app.example,https://admin.example'` for services and plugins, or pass `cors: { origin: [...] }` to `defineService` / `createPluginService` (or `.withCors({ origin: [...] })` on builders). Unset origins deny cross-origin browser calls, and wildcard plus credentials fails `build()`. Generated CLI/Aspire helpers inject your enabled web apps' origins automatically, so scaffolded projects keep working.
- **#2220: `defineService()` requires an auth policy.** A missing policy used to mean "public". Pass `auth: { authn: { authenticator }, authz: { authorizer } }` (authorization is optional), or, for a genuinely public service, `auth: { public: true, reason: '…' }` with a non-blank reason. The service README and CHANGELOG have the before/after.
- **#2177: signout is owner-scoped.** Anonymous signout returns `401`; `sessionId` must be one of the caller's own sessions; `everywhere` now revokes all of the caller's sessions. Revoking someone else's session needs `revokeSession` with `auth:sessions:revoke`. Custom `AuthSessionStorePort`, `KvOAuthStore` and `BetterAuthInstance` implementations gain one method each (see the auth docs callout "Breaking in 0.0.8: migrating signout callers"). `plugin auth session list` needs a credential.
- **#2125: plugin composition is validated.** Unknown contribution keys fail, every declared plugin dependency must be composed, and `@netscript/plugin-triggers` no longer declares pseudo-dependencies on the `*-core` libraries. Migration notes are in the plugin README and reference page.
- **#2189: auth cookies are stricter.** `HttpOnly=false` and insecure custom-name cookies are refused outside an explicit development policy; `KvOAuthCookieOptions.httpOnly` is typed `true`.

It wraps `writeFreshRouteManifestSync` through the shared app selector, with deterministic and idempotent output and reconstruction after a route change, and the live help docs are updated. This proves #2009's box 5. **Closes nothing:** the page-removal leaf (triad deletion with router reconciliation) starts now.

It backfills retention for the KV runtime-store entries that predate #2286 (legacy terminal saga and trigger families). Each pass is capped and checkpointed, restart-safe and idempotent, with batched owner reads and atomic race protection, and never touches open instances. Operator instructions are in the PR. **Closes nothing:** #2109's long-lived-store run is coordinator-owned, and #2108 (KV-only install) is in #2300.

**Merged: #2239** (`fix(auth)`: typed WorkOS sealed-session user for #2231; squash `d060f07`). A regression test parses the scaffold-init argv with both real CLI command definitions across all databases. The init gate's timeout works again on the local-source path.

**Merged: #2311** (`docs`: internal-procedure lane recipe for #2064; squash `a2598c5`). Opus PASS at the merged head `29761e42d` (confirm after a one-line import fix), required CI and both `scaffold.runtime` tiers green. The recipe covers how a service exposes an internal procedure, how another service or background resource calls it with #2279's provisioned credential, what is refused (anonymous and OpenAPI), and rotation. Its snippets are executable, with a generated-carrier proof and no secret values anywhere. **Next:** the coordinator runs the provisioned recipe under the runtime lease and reconciles #2064.

**Merged: #2310** (`fix(workers)`: `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` reaches the runtime, for #1369; squash `f7fc419`). Opus PASS at the merged head `70b5db5c6` (third review), required CI and both `scaffold.runtime` tiers green. The worker passes the resolved concurrency to its queue listener and reports it on completed job spans. A generated-project receipt gate in both runtime tiers proves the declared value takes effect; its comparison normalises string telemetry (`"2"`) and number values to validated integers. The canonical env name and docs had already landed in #2167. With #2296 (streams root exports), both halves of #1369 are merged.

**Merged: #2314** (`feat(cli)`: `netscript ui:remove page` for #2009; squash `504c4cd`). Opus PASS at the merged head `df7b827bf` (third review), required CI and both `scaffold.runtime` tiers green. It removes a generated page's files and reconciles `router.ts` and the route manifest, keeping unrelated authored routes. It refuses files that diverge from their generated shape, supports a dry run, is idempotent, rewrites the router before deleting files (so an interrupted run never leaves a dangling registration), and prunes empty nested route directories. Help and route docs are updated. With #2294 (`generate routes`), the coordinator reconciles #2009's boxes next.

**Merged: #2318** (`test(fresh)`: native chat test cancellation, **closes #2317** (CLOSED); squash `37cd4ba`). Opus PASS at the merged head `45b767b4a`, with required CI and both `scaffold.runtime` tiers green. **Root cause:** a Deno 2.9.5 runtime defect. When a `fetch` `Response` is garbage-collected before abort, the abort no longer cancels the server's streaming body (denoland/deno#37006). The test now waits on the real server cancellation event and retains the response. Proof: 50 of 50 focused runs, plus 20 of 20 parallel full Fresh suites (6,180 passes). This flake had been failing `check-test` on most PRs since about 11:00Z; it is now off `main`. The production side (Deno-hosted transports) is #2324, fixed in #2325 (in review).

The docs-accuracy gate now fails if either retired caveat wording returns (the `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` workaround clause, or the unsupported streams-helpers caveat), with negative controls. The one remaining `WORKER_CONCURRENCY` literal is the intentional, tested 0.0.8 deprecation alias. All 9 boxes map to evidence across #2167, #2296, #2310 and this PR. #1369: CLOSED unticked=0.
