issues.title: Spec: Collector workspace
issues.body:
**Spec file:** [docs/planning/collector-workspace/spec.md](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/collector-workspace/spec.md) on `feature/ui-workspace-redesign`

**Status:** ready for implementation planning. Revised 2026-10-11 for prices, Deck cost and exports after they merged into `dev`. Revised again the same day for Location management from [Decide drag and Location ordering](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/issues/46) and for the visual system from [Decide responsive visual system](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/issues/47).

**Sources:** [Collector workspace selection and presentation](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/tcg-collection-tracker/wayfinder/resolutions/29-decide-collector-workspace-selection-and-presentation.md) (product rules, owner-confirmed 2026-10-09), [ADR 0005](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/adr/0005-collector-workspace-multi-source-direction.md) (multi-source direction), the [collector workspace prototype](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/tcg-collection-tracker/wayfinder/prototypes/collector-workspace/README.md) (Variant A), the [UI redesign map](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/tcg-collection-tracker/wayfinder/ui-redesign-map.md), and the [card prices and Deck exports spec](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/card-prices-and-deck-exports/spec.md), whose pricing and export rules this workspace must keep. Location ordering and management follow [the drag and Location ordering resolution](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/tcg-collection-tracker/wayfinder/resolutions/27-decide-drag-and-location-ordering.md), and the visual system follows [the responsive visual system resolution](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/tcg-collection-tracker/wayfinder/resolutions/28-decide-responsive-visual-system.md). This spec resolves [Decide atomic multi-source inventory operations](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/issues/49).

## Problem Statement

My cards live in many physical places: binders, boxes, Decks. Today I manage them one Storage Leaf at a time, as rows of Holdings with quantities. I can't see my collection the way I see it on the table, as cards. When I want to gather copies from several places, for example every Charizard from my binder and my trade box, I have to repeat the same Move once per source. If I make a mistake, I have to undo each Move separately. Filtering by card category or elemental type isn't possible. On a phone, the workspace isn't built for picking several cards and acting on them together.

## Solution

A redesigned collector workspace shows the Collection as a gallery of small card tiles, one tile per copy. The desktop keeps the Location sidebar visible. Above the gallery, one aligned toolbar holds Search and Filters on the left and Sort, card size and name visibility on the right. I can select tiles across any number of Storage Leaves by click, Ctrl/Cmd-click, Shift-click, marquee or (on mobile) Select mode. Then I can Move them to one destination or remove them from the Collection in a single all-or-nothing operation that one Undo reverses. I can add Locations directly from the sidebar tree. On mobile, a left drawer holds the Location tree and a right drawer holds Filters & display. The inspector shows the inspected card's price, an opt-in Prices toggle adds prices under the tiles, and an open Deck shows its Estimated Deck Cost and Export menu in the heading.

Holdings stay fungible quantities. A tile is a selectable unit of a Holding's quantity, not a durable record of a physical copy.

## User Stories

### Browsing the gallery

1. As a collector, I want All owned to show my whole Collection as card tiles, one per copy, so that I see my cards the way I store them.
2. As a collector, I want copies of the same Card Edition kept next to each other, so that I can count and compare them at a glance.
3. As a collector, I want every copy shown by scrolling with no artificial cap, stack, fan or "+N" overlay, so that nothing is hidden from me.
4. As a collector, I want to open a Storage Leaf from the sidebar and see only its tiles, so that the gallery matches what is physically in that binder, box or Deck.
5. As a collector, I want each tile in All owned to show its source Location caption even when names are hidden, so that I know where every copy lives.
6. As a collector, I want the source caption omitted inside a Storage Leaf, so that tiles aren't cluttered with information I already know.
7. As a collector, I want card names hidden by default and switchable on, so that the gallery is artwork-first but I can read names when I need them.
8. As a collector, I want small and medium card sizes, so that I can trade density for detail.
9. As a collector, I want the heading to show copy and Card Edition counts with correct singular and plural forms, so that the totals read naturally.
10. As a collector with a 25,000-Holding Collection, I want the gallery to scroll smoothly, so that a large Collection stays usable.
11. As a collector, I want a tile's hover title and accessible label to include the card name, copy number and full Location path, so that I can identify any tile without names shown.

### Searching, filtering and sorting

12. As a collector, I want to search my cards by name from the toolbar, so that I can find a card quickly.
13. As a collector, I want to filter by set, so that I can focus on one release.
14. As a collector, I want to filter by category (Pokémon, Trainer, Energy), so that I can separate card kinds.
15. As a collector, I want to filter by elemental type, so that I can gather cards for a type-themed Deck.
16. As a collector, I want filters to combine independently, so that I can narrow by set, category and type together.
17. As a collector, I want Clear filters to reset filters only, leaving sort, card size and name visibility alone, so that I don't lose display choices.
18. As a collector, I want an indicator when filters are active, so that I know the gallery is narrowed.
19. As a collector, I want to sort by name (A–Z default), set plus collector number, or quantity, ascending or descending where applicable, so that I can order the gallery my way.
20. As a collector, I want quantity sort to use the Card Edition's total in the current view, so that the order reflects what I'm looking at.
21. As a collector, I want copies within a Card Edition ordered by source Location, so that the gallery is stable and predictable.
22. As a collector, I want sort, filters, card size and name visibility remembered between visits in this browser, so that the workspace opens the way I left it.
23. As a collector, I want search text and selection to reset between visits, so that I start each visit with a clean slate.

### Selecting

24. As a desktop collector, I want a click to select one tile, so that selection is quick.
25. As a desktop collector, I want clicking the only selected tile to deselect it, so that I can undo a stray click.
26. As a desktop collector, I want Ctrl/Cmd-click to toggle tiles, so that I can build a group across Locations.
27. As a desktop collector, I want Shift-click to select the displayed range left to right, then top to bottom, so that I can grab a run of tiles.
28. As a desktop collector, I want to drag a marquee from empty grid space to replace the selection, so that I can select an area.
29. As a desktop collector, I want Ctrl/Cmd-marquee to add to the selection, so that I can combine areas.
30. As a collector, I want clicking empty space or pressing Escape to clear the selection, so that deselecting is easy.
31. As a collector, I want a selection to span Storage Leaves, so that one action can gather copies from several places.
32. As a collector, I want sorting to keep my selection, so that I can reorder without losing work.
33. As a collector, I want changing search, filters or Location to clear my selection, so that I never act on tiles I can no longer see.
34. As a collector, I want a selection bar showing selected copies, Card Editions and Locations with correct plurals, so that I know what I'm about to act on.

### Inspecting

35. As a desktop collector, I want the inspection panel reserved but empty while idle, so that the layout doesn't jump.
36. As a desktop collector, I want hovering a tile to preview it only when nothing is selected, so that hover doesn't fight my selection.
37. As a collector, I want the inspector to show the last-clicked selected Card Edition, so that I can check a card while building a group.
38. As a collector, I want the inspector to show set, number, category, type, the copy's Location path, copies there and total owned, so that I have the facts I need.

### Moving and removing

39. As a collector, I want Actions (Move, Inventory Removal, Clear) whenever tiles are selected, so that every operation has a non-drag path.
40. As a collector, I want Move to open a searchable folder-style Location explorer, so that I can find the destination in a deep tree.
41. As a collector, I want Organizational Locations to expand in the explorer and only Storage Leaves (including Decks) to be selectable, so that I can't pick an invalid destination.
42. As a collector, I want the explorer to show the destination's full path and the number of copies that will actually move before I confirm, so that there are no surprises.
43. As a collector, I want copies already at the destination to stay put and not count as moved, so that a mixed group behaves sensibly.
44. As a collector, I want Move confirmation disabled when every selected copy is already at the destination, so that I can't submit a no-op.
45. As a desktop collector, I want to drag a selected tile to carry the whole selection, so that drag works on groups.
46. As a desktop collector, I want dragging an unselected tile to carry only that tile, so that a quick drag doesn't grab an old selection.
47. As a desktop collector, I want a compact copy and Card Edition count badge while dragging, plus highlighted valid destinations, so that I know what I'm carrying and where it can go.
48. As a desktop collector, I want dropping on a valid Storage Leaf to Move immediately, with Undo, so that drag stays fast.
49. As a collector, I want a group Move to succeed completely or change nothing, so that my inventory is never half-moved.
50. As a collector, I want a failed Move to keep my selection and name the affected source Location, so that I can fix the problem and retry.
51. As a collector, I want a successful Move or Removal to clear my selection, so that I'm ready for the next task.
52. As a collector, I want Inventory Removal to confirm each Card Edition, quantity and source Location, so that I know exactly what leaves my Collection.
53. As a collector, I want a multi-source Inventory Removal to be one atomic operation, so that it never partly applies.
54. As a collector moving thousands of copies, I want progress feedback while the selection is staged, so that I know the app is working.

### Undo

55. As a collector, I want one Undo for a group operation that restores every copy to its original source together, so that a mistake is one click to reverse.
56. As a collector, I want an Undo that can't apply cleanly to change nothing and say it's unavailable, so that recovery never makes things worse.
57. As a collector, I want to dismiss an unavailable newest Undo to reach older eligible ones, so that one blocked record doesn't trap the rest.
58. As a collector, I want the existing newest-five, ten-minute Undo policy kept, so that recovery behaves as it does today.

### Locations

59. As a collector, I want the desktop Location sidebar always visible, so that navigation and drop targets are always there.
60. As a collector, I want folder disclosures in the tree, so that I can collapse parts I'm not using.
61. As a collector, I want a plus beside the Locations heading to create a top-level Location, so that adding storage is one step.
62. As a desktop collector, I want an Add child plus on eligible rows on hover or keyboard focus, so that the tree stays clean until I need it.
63. As a mobile collector, I want Add child controls always visible at a full touch size, so that I can reach them without hover.
64. As a collector, I want Deck rows to have no Add child control, so that the rule that Decks have no children is clear.
65. As a collector, I want Add child to preselect its parent in the Name-and-parent form, so that I don't pick it twice.
66. As a collector adding a child to a stocked Storage Leaf, I want the choices to move its Holdings into the new child, create a separate Unsorted child, or cancel, so that my cards always stay in a Storage Leaf.
67. As a collector, I want the new Location selected and its ancestors expanded after creation, so that I can start using it at once.
68. As a collector, I want long Location names to stay readable in the sidebar, with the full name on hover, so that similar names don't blur together.

### Mobile

69. As a mobile collector, I want a left header control opening the Location drawer, so that navigation is one tap away.
70. As a mobile collector, I want a right "Filters & display" control opening filters, sort, card size and name visibility, so that the gallery has room.
71. As a mobile collector, I want drawer changes to apply immediately and stay after closing, so that the drawers feel direct.
72. As a mobile collector, I want search always reachable in the header, so that finding a card doesn't need a drawer.
73. As a mobile collector, I want a normal tap to open inspection in a sheet, so that browsing is simple.
74. As a mobile collector, I want a visible Select mode where taps toggle tiles across Locations, so that I can build groups by touch.
75. As a mobile collector, I want the selected count and Actions in a compact strip, with details on demand, so that the gallery stays visible.
76. As a mobile collector, I want vertical scrolling to keep working in Select mode, so that selection doesn't trap the page.
77. As a mobile collector, I want header controls at least 44×44 px, so that they're easy to tap.

### Keyboard and accessibility

78. As a keyboard user, I want to focus tiles and toggle them with Space in selection mode, so that I can select without a mouse.
79. As a keyboard user, I want a complete Move path through Actions, so that I never need drag.
80. As a screen reader user, I want every tile, control and dialog labelled, and focus returned to the opener when a drawer or dialog closes, so that I can follow the workspace.

### Consistency and safety

81. As a collector with two tabs open, I want an operation based on stale quantities to fail without changes, so that I never Move cards that already moved.
82. As a collector on a flaky connection, I want a retried commit to apply once, so that a retry never doubles a Move.
83. As a collector, I want existing single-source Move, Removal and Undo to keep working, so that nothing I rely on regresses.

### Prices, Deck cost and exports

84. As a collector, I want the inspector to show the exact Card Edition's USD price with its age, a stale label or an explicit unavailable state, so that I can judge the value without mistaking a missing quote for $0.
85. As a collector, I want a Prices display toggle, off by default, that shows each visible tile's Card Edition price under it, so that I can browse by value when I want to.
86. As a collector, I want prices loaded only for tiles on screen, so that browsing a large Collection doesn't fetch prices for cards I haven't looked at.
87. As a collector, I want the Prices toggle remembered with my other display preferences, so that the gallery opens the way I left it.
88. As a collector viewing a Deck, I want its Estimated Deck Cost with Pricing Coverage and stale and unknown-age counts in the heading, so that I see what the Deck is worth and how complete that figure is.
89. As a collector viewing a Deck, I want an Export menu with Pokémon TCG Live text and TCGplayer Mass Entry, so that I can export without leaving the gallery.
90. As a collector, I want Deck exports in the workspace to block, fall back and warn exactly as they do on the Decks page, so that no card is dropped or substituted.
91. As a collector on the Decks page, I want an Open in workspace link for each Deck, so that I can go from checks and publishing to the Deck's cards.
92. As a collector, I want a "Report a problem with this card's data" link in the inspector, so that I can report a wrong price mapping or export detail where I notice it.
93. As a collector on a large screen, I want the gallery to use the full width beside the sidebar, with more cards per row as the screen grows, so that space isn't wasted.

### Managing Locations

94. As a collector, I want sibling Locations sorted naturally A–Z, so that "Binder 2" comes before "Binder 10".
95. As a collector, I want a settings gear beside the Locations heading that opens Manage locations, so that all Location upkeep is in one place.
96. As a collector, I want Manage locations to list my whole tree with Rename, Add child and Delete on each row, so that I can edit any Location without opening it first.
97. As a collector, I want to drag a Location by its ☰ handle onto another Location to nest it there, so that reorganizing storage is direct.
98. As a collector, I want a Top level drop zone, so that I can move a Location out of every folder.
99. As a mobile collector, I want the handle drag to work with touch, so that I can reorganize on my phone.
100. As a collector, I want invalid targets (the Location itself, its descendants, Decks, its current parent, anything past 12 levels) dimmed and refusing the drop, so that I can't make an impossible move.
101. As a collector, I want every Location move confirmed with the new full path, so that a stray drop never reorganizes my storage.
102. As a collector moving a Location into a stocked Storage Leaf, I want the confirmation to explain that its cards move into a new Unsorted child, so that no card is left in a folder.
103. As a keyboard or touch user, I want tapping or activating the handle to open a Move picker of valid parents, so that I never need to drag.
104. As a collector, I want Rename to reject a name already used by a sibling, ignoring case, so that the tree stays unambiguous.
105. As a collector, I want Delete limited to empty Locations with no children and confirmed by typing the name, so that I can't lose cards or structure by accident.
106. As a collector, I want to rename a Deck and move it to another folder, so that its record follows the physical box.
107. As a collector, I want sidebar rows to accept only card drops, so that dragging cards never moves a Location by mistake.

### Look and feel

108. As a collector, I want the workspace in the Prize gold dark theme, so that PrizeCheck has a consistent look.
109. As a collector, I want the Names toggle to also show each card's set and collector number on a second line, so that I can tell printings apart without opening the inspector.
110. As a collector, I want every tile's hover title and screen-reader label to include its set and number, so that the information is there even with Names off.
111. As a collector, I want selected tiles marked by a ring separated from the card by a dark gap, plus a check badge, so that selection is obvious even on yellow-bordered cards and doesn't rely on colour.
112. As a collector, I want card-shaped placeholders while the gallery loads, so that the layout doesn't jump.
113. As a collector, I want a banner with Reload when my collection changed in another tab, so that I never act on out-of-date tiles without knowing.
114. As a collector, I want errors shown where they happened, so that I know what to fix.
115. As a keyboard user, I want a visible focus ring on every control and tile, so that I always know where I am.
116. As a collector who prefers reduced motion, I want transitions turned off, so that the interface doesn't animate.
117. As a collector with low vision, I want text and control outlines to meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, so that I can read and find everything.

## Implementation Decisions

### Domain boundary

- Holdings remain fungible quantities of one Card Edition in one Storage Leaf. No copy IDs, copy-specific fields, or per-copy persistence are added. A tile is identified on the client only by Storage Leaf, Card Edition and an ordinal within that Holding's quantity. Organizational Locations still can't hold Holdings. A Deck is still an ordinary Storage Leaf source and destination.
- Selection is held as a count per Holding (Storage Leaf + Card Edition → selected quantity), not as a list of tile identities. This keeps very large selections compact. It also maps directly onto manifest items.

### Multi-source Move, Removal and Undo (resolves #49)

The existing manifest flow is extended rather than replaced: start, stage in bounded batches, commit once. This keeps the existing atomicity, owner lock, staging limits and idempotency.

- **Manifest scope.** Starting a manifest no longer requires a source. An optional source is still accepted for compatibility: when present, items that omit a source default to it. One live manifest per owner, the one-hour staging expiry and the 500-item batch limit stay unchanged.
- **Manifest items.** Each staged item carries `source_id`, `edition_id`, `quantity` (decimal string) and `expected_version`. Items are unique per (source, Card Edition). Restaging an identical item is a no-op; restaging a conflicting one is rejected as a duplicate, as today.
- **Commit (Move).** One destination Storage Leaf. Items whose source is the destination are excluded as already there and don't count. If every item is excluded, the commit fails with a no-op error and changes nothing. All remaining items are validated together under the owner lock against one snapshot covering every involved source and the destination: each source must still be a Storage Leaf, each expected version must match, each source quantity must suffice, and the destination must not overflow. Any failure aborts the whole operation.
- **Commit (Inventory Removal).** No destination. The same all-or-nothing validation across sources.
- **Failure detail.** Conflict errors keep their existing codes (stale Holding, insufficient quantity, overflow, Location not found). The error body also names the affected source Storage Leaf and Card Edition, so the UI can say which Location to check. Selection is preserved on failure.
- **Result.** Move and Removal results report moved Card Edition count, moved copy count, source Location count, already-at-destination copy count and the new owner revision. The existing fields keep their meaning.
- **Idempotency.** Unchanged: the per-owner idempotency key with a command digest, and replay returns the original result.
- **Undo record.** The payload stores per-item source, Card Edition and quantity. The record's single-source field becomes optional; it is populated when one source was involved, so existing records and clients keep working. The Undo list adds a source Location count.
- **Undo apply.** All-or-nothing across every source. It's incompatible, and changes nothing, if any original source is no longer a Storage Leaf, the destination lacks the moved quantity, or any restore would overflow. The newest-only rule, newest-five retention, ten-minute expiry and dismiss-to-reach-older behaviour are unchanged.
- **Migration.** A schema migration adds the source to manifest items and Undo payload handling and relaxes the manifest's required source. Existing single-source Undo records are read as payload items whose source is the record's source. The generated TypeScript client is regenerated, and the generated-client check covers it.
- **Performance.** The existing budget holds: a 25,000-Edition Move, including staging, completes within two minutes with progress. Validation and transfer stay set-based in one transaction.

### Collection read for the gallery

- The gallery needs Holding-level rows (Storage Leaf + Card Edition + quantity + version + display data), not only per-Edition totals. The Collection read gains a Holding-level listing scoped to All owned or one Storage Leaf. It uses cursor pagination, name search, set, category and elemental type filters, and sorts by name, set plus collector number, or quantity (the Card Edition total within the current view). Rows are ordered by Card Edition, then source Location.
- Category (Pokémon, Trainer, Energy) and elemental type become stored, filterable catalog attributes of a Card Printing. The catalog import already reads category. Storing both requires a catalog migration and a re-import or backfill.
- Responses keep carrying the owner revision so the workspace can detect staleness and refetch.

### Workspace UI

- The workspace replaces the current Locations/Holdings management view as the signed-in collector's main inventory page. Catalog search for adding cards, Deck checks, publishing and operations pages are unchanged.
- **Rendering.** Tiles are expanded client-side from Holding quantities and rendered with viewport virtualization so a 25,000-Holding Collection stays responsive. Shift-range and marquee hit-testing are computed from the gallery's layout model (row, column, tile size), not from mounted DOM nodes, because offscreen tiles aren't mounted.
- **Interactions.** Every rule in [the workspace resolution](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/tcg-collection-tracker/wayfinder/resolutions/29-decide-collector-workspace-selection-and-presentation.md) is normative for interactions: selection, inspection precedence, Actions, the Move explorer, drag, mobile drawers, Select mode, keyboard paths and Location creation.
- **Move paths.** A drag-drop onto a valid Storage Leaf commits immediately and offers Undo. Actions → Move goes through the explorer with a full path and actual moving count before confirmation. This adopts the reviewed picker confirmation that the resolution left to specification.
- **Location creation.** This reuses the existing Name-and-parent create contract, including the existing atomic stocked-leaf conversion choices. No backend change is needed.
- **Location order.** Every Location tree (sidebar, mobile drawer, Move explorer, Manage locations) sorts siblings in natural A–Z order, numeric-aware and case-insensitive. No order is stored.
- **Manage locations.** A gear beside the root + opens a centred panel on desktop and a full-screen sheet on mobile. Each row has a ☰ handle, Rename, Add child (not on Decks) and Delete. The panel's drag, confirmation and picker rules are those of [the drag and Location ordering resolution](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/tcg-collection-tracker/wayfinder/resolutions/27-decide-drag-and-location-ordering.md). Reparenting uses the existing Location edit command, including its stale-version check and stocked-leaf Unsorted conversion. Rename and Delete use the existing commands and rules.
- **Handle drag.** The handle drag uses pointer events, not native HTML drag-and-drop, so the same code serves mouse and touch. A press that doesn't pass a small movement threshold is a tap and opens the Move picker; Enter and Space do the same. The handle sets `touch-action: none` and is at least 44×44 px on mobile.
- **Deck edit command.** Decks currently reject Location edits (`DECK_REQUIRES_DECK_COMMAND`). A Deck rename and move command is added with the same stale-version, sibling-name, depth and idempotency rules as Location edits. A Deck can't become a parent. Deck deletion is not part of this command.
- **No Location Undo.** Location changes have no Undo. Card Undo records that a Location change invalidates show "Undo unavailable" and can be dismissed, as today.
- **Preferences.** Sort, filters, card size and name visibility persist in browser storage per user on that device. Account-bound preferences are deferred. Search text and selection aren't persisted.
- **Sidebar sizing.** The desktop sidebar is 212 px at every desktop width, Add child overlays the row end rather than reserving width, and names carry a hover title. Mobile header controls and Add child controls are at least 44 px tall, and the mobile header Location control is 44×44 px.
- **Counts.** All copy, Card Edition, Location and selection counts use singular and plural forms.
- **Design variables.** The workspace introduces the app's shared design variables, defined in [the responsive visual system resolution](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/tcg-collection-tracker/wayfinder/resolutions/28-decide-responsive-visual-system.md): colour roles, a 4 px spacing scale, corner radii and tile sizes. No component uses a hardcoded colour. Other pages move onto the variables when they are redesigned.
- **Themes.** Dark only. Prize gold is the default and only shipped theme; a theme is one set of colour-role values selected by an attribute on the app root, so the Grass and Water values from the prototype and later energy-type presets can be added without touching components. A user-facing theme picker is not part of this work.
- **Type.** The system font, with tabular numerals for counts, prices, collector numbers and quantities.
- **Accessibility baseline.** WCAG 2.2 AA contrast in every theme, with a separate control-outline colour at 3:1 or better. Visible focus rings everywhere. Targets at least 44 px on mobile and 24 px on desktop. Transitions of 150 ms or less, and none under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Selected, stale, unavailable and error states never rely on colour alone.
- **Selected tiles.** A dark gap, an accent ring and a filled check badge inside the card's top-right corner.
- **Names line.** The Names toggle shows the card name and, on a second line, its set name and collector number. Hover titles and accessible labels always include set and number.
- **Feedback states.** Card-shaped placeholder tiles while loading. Inline errors in the dialog or form where they happened. A stale-data banner with Reload above the gallery, using the owner revision the reads already return. The success and Undo toast at the bottom centre on desktop and above the Actions strip on mobile.
- **Visual pass.** The "Move here" confirmation button in Manage locations is restyled; the owner flagged it as looking odd.
- **Layout width.** The app-wide stylesheet caps `main` at 900 px and centres it. The workspace must not inherit that cap. The gallery fills the width beside the sidebar, side padding shrinks on large screens (30 px, then 20 px from 1550 px, then 16 px from 2200 px), and cards per row follow the available width at a fixed tile size.
- **Prototype code.** The development-only prototype modules are removed once the production workspace lands. The production build must not include prototype code or styles.

### Prices, Deck cost and exports

- The [card prices and Deck exports spec](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/blob/feature/ui-workspace-redesign/docs/planning/card-prices-and-deck-exports/spec.md) stays authoritative for every pricing and export rule. The workspace reuses its existing price, Deck cost, export and metadata-report components and contracts; it adds no new pricing or export API.
- **Inspector.** It shows the inspected Card Edition's price through the existing price component, with age, stale and unavailable labels.
- **Prices toggle.** A Prices display preference, off by default and stored with the other display preferences, adds the Card Edition price under each tile. Copies of the same Card Edition share one price. Only tiles mounted by the virtualized gallery render a price, so only those count as price access. The existing component's batching (at most 64 Editions per request, two requests in flight) is kept.
- **No price sort, filter or totals.** Each of these would need a price for every Card Edition in view, which the access-only refresh rule forbids. A selection subtotal with coverage is a possible follow-up that needs its own server endpoint.
- **Deck heading.** When the open Storage Leaf is a Deck, the heading shows the existing Estimated Deck Cost summary (subtotal, Pricing Coverage, stale and unknown-age counts) and an Export menu that opens the existing TCG Live and TCGplayer Mass Entry panels. Cost and exports use the server's complete Deck read, not the tiles currently loaded.
- **Decks page.** It keeps Deck checks, cost, exports and Publish, and adds an Open in workspace link per Deck.
- **Metadata reports.** The inspector links to the existing metadata report form, preset to the inspected Card Edition. The catalog search entry point is unchanged.

### Prototype-derived shapes

From the prototype, trimmed. The selection and operation shapes the UI sends:

```ts
// One selected group, as staged into a manifest item.
type SelectedGroup = { source_id: string; edition_id: string; quantity: string; expected_version: number };

// Move preview shown before confirmation.
type MovePreview = {
  destination_id: string;
  moving: number;          // copies whose source ≠ destination
  alreadyThere: number;    // copies whose source = destination; stay put, not counted
};                         // confirm disabled when moving === 0
```

## Testing Decisions

- **What a good test is.** Tests check external behaviour only. In the browser, that means what a collector sees and can do. At the API, it means HTTP responses and resulting Holding quantities. Tests never assert component internals, CSS class names, the selection data structure or SQL.
- **Seam 1 — browser.** Playwright page tests against the real local stack: auth, API, database. They cover the gallery, filters and sort, preference persistence, every selection gesture (including Shift-range and marquee across virtualized offscreen rows), inspection precedence, Move via Actions and via drag, multi-source Move and Removal, Undo, Location creation from the tree, mobile drawers and Select mode at 375×812, keyboard-only Move, and the singular-count copy. Prior art: `moves.spec.ts` (Move by drag and by control), `location-conversion.spec.ts`, `location-tree.spec.ts`, `mobile-journey.spec.ts`, `holdings.spec.ts` and `collection.spec.ts`.
- **Prices and Deck tools in the browser.** Playwright tests cover:
  - the inspector price with stale and unavailable states
  - the Prices toggle, its persistence, and that only on-screen tiles request prices
  - the Deck heading's cost and coverage
  - TCG Live and Mass Entry exports opened from the Deck heading, including a blocked export
  - Open in workspace from the Decks page
  - the inspector's metadata report link

  Prior art: `prices.spec.ts`, `price-refresh.spec.ts`, `live-export.spec.ts`, `mass-entry.spec.ts` and `metadata-review.spec.ts`. The existing API tests for prices and exports stay as they are, since no API changes.
- **Managing Locations in the browser.** Playwright tests cover:
  - natural sibling order
  - handle drag onto a row and onto Top level with a mouse, and with touch emulation at 375×812
  - invalid targets refusing a drop
  - the confirmation, including the stocked-leaf Unsorted conversion
  - a tap and a keypress opening the Move picker
  - Rename with a duplicate sibling name rejected
  - Delete with the typed-name confirmation
  - Deck rename and move
  - a stale edit from a second tab failing without changes

  Prior art: `location-tree.spec.ts` and `location-conversion.spec.ts`.
- **Look and feel in the browser.** Playwright tests cover:
  - the Names toggle showing name, set and number, and labels including set and number with Names off
  - the selected state showing a badge, not only a colour change
  - placeholder tiles before the gallery's first data arrives
  - the stale-data banner after a change from a second tab, and Reload
  - focus rings visible on tiles and controls during keyboard navigation
  - no transitions under emulated reduced motion
  - an automated contrast check, such as axe, on the workspace with no AA violations

  Prior art: `mobile-journey.spec.ts` for viewport emulation, and `review-fixes.spec.ts`.
- **Seam 2 — HTTP API.** Pytest against the API covers the multi-source contract:
  - atomic success across three sources
  - already-at-destination exclusion and the all-no-op rejection
  - stale-version, insufficient-quantity, overflow and non-leaf failures with no mutation and the affected source named in the error
  - idempotent replay and key reuse
  - multi-source Removal
  - the Deck rename and move command: success, stale version, duplicate sibling name, Deck or descendant as the target parent, depth limit, stocked-leaf conversion and idempotent replay (prior art: `test_location_tree.py`, `test_location_conversion.py`, `test_decks.py`)
  - multi-source Undo, including incompatibility when one source became Organizational
  - coexistence with single-source manifests and pre-existing single-source Undo records after migration
  - the Holding-level Collection listing with category and elemental type filters and the specified sort order

  Prior art: `test_moves.py`, `test_inventory_undo.py`, `test_collection.py`, `test_holdings.py` and `test_location_conversion.py`.
- **Load proof.** The existing 25,000-Edition Move fixture and local-capacity validation are re-run with a selection spanning several sources, against the same two-minute budget.
- **No new seams.** Workspace state isn't split into a separately unit-tested module for this work.
- **Gates.** `npm run verify` is the full gate. Workers iterate on single tests and run the full gate once at the end.

## Out of Scope

- Durable per-copy records, copy IDs or copy-specific metadata.
- Dedicated deck-building UI.
- Account-bound display preferences (card size, name visibility, sort, filters persist only in the browser).
- A light theme, a user-facing theme picker, the energy-type preset themes, and custom colours.
- Moving pages other than the workspace onto the shared design variables.
- A wordmark font or logo.
- Manual sibling ordering and drag-to-reorder. Order is natural A–Z.
- Undo for Location changes.
- Deleting Decks, including what happens to their Published Decks.
- Extending the workspace to catalog search, reporting, publishing and discovery, and owner controls.
- Price sorting, price filters, and value totals for a selection, a Location or the Collection.
- Changes to pricing, Deck cost or export rules, and Published Deck pricing and exports.
- Changes to Deck construction checks, Published Decks, or catalog import beyond storing category and elemental type.

## Further Notes

- Native HTML drag-and-drop and real touch gestures couldn't be automated in the prototype harness, so the browser tests must actually exercise drop and touch. Playwright drag and touch emulation are the minimum; record any remaining gap as a manual check in the launch checklist.
- Screen-reader output, contrast and full keyboard traversal weren't verified in the prototype. They are acceptance items here.
- The prototype's four owner-review observations (sidebar truncation, the duplicated mobile drawer title, the 36 px mobile control, and "1 editions") were fixed in the prototype on 2026-10-10. The corresponding rules are carried into the decisions above.
- **Revision 2026-10-11.** Prices, Deck cost and exports merged into `dev` in [ry-cen/prizecheck#78](https://github.com/ry-cen/prizecheck/pull/78). The owner chose: the inspector plus an opt-in Prices toggle for tiles, no price sort, filter or totals, Deck cost and Export in the Deck heading, the Decks page kept with an Open in workspace link, and a metadata report link in the inspector.
- The MVP specification's single-source Move/Removal/Undo text should be updated to point here when this spec is accepted. Per ADR 0005, the current single-source behavior stays authoritative until this work lands.

issues.title: Evaluate LLM security scan and fix when appropriate
issues.body: Context: * You should never pass untrusted code through jsdoctor. * This project works on security issues in the open. * This reported issues might well be incorrect. * At this time, jsdoctor should keep the API stable **prompt**: > Do a security scan of each file in jsdoctor. Be aggressive about reporting possible issues. Rate each issue for its severity and probability that it is real. Write a .md report of any issues found. Give the CWE, Importance, Confidence, Location, Description, and Proposed fix. Use a separate agent per file. After all the reports are done, create a SECURITY_SCAN_SUMMARY.md and list all the issues ranked by first Confidence and second by Importance. Do not use security scanning tools. Using other tools is allowed. The agents should directly inspect the code. For each entry, add a patch inline in the document for the fix. Evaluate the code with the assumption that it will only be used with python >= 3.14. ### 1. jsdoc.py.md - CWE-436 (Interpretation Conflict) / Logic Flaw - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Line 55 (`r"(?:\s|\A)(?P@\w+)\b"`) - **Description**: The regular expression designed to find JSDoc flags matches any `@word` that is preceded by whitespace, regardless of its position in a line. If a developer uses decorators in code snippets (e.g., ` @decorator`) or includes references / email addresses (e.g., `mention me @username`), the parser immediately truncates the description and consumes the remainder of the text as a tag value. This severely corrupts normal documentation blocks. - **Proposed Fix**: JSDoc block flags should only be recognized at the beginning of a line. Alter the regular expression to use the multiline flag and match the line start (with optional leading whitespace): `re.finditer(r"^[ \t]*(?P@\w+)\b", text, re.MULTILINE)`. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -58,3 +58,3 @@ - parts = comment_text.split("\n\n") + parts = re.split(r'\n\s*\n', comment_text) ``` ### 2. jsdoc.py.md - CWE-1284 (Improper Validation of Syntactic Structure) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Line 60 (`parts = comment_text.split("\n\n")`) - **Description**: The code splits sections strictly using exactly two newline characters (`\n\n`). However, it is extremely common for JSDoc comment blocks to contain empty lines that are indented with spaces (e.g. `\n \n`), often introduced by a text editor's auto-formatter or upstream stripping logic that removes leading `*` characters. In these cases, `split("\n\n")` will fail to recognize the section break, improperly merging disjoint structural sections into one. - **Proposed Fix**: Use regular expressions to split on consecutive newlines regardless of intermediate horizontal whitespace. For instance: `parts = re.split(r'\n[ \t]*\n', comment_text)`. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -48,3 +48,3 @@ -def _match_flags(text: str) -> Iterator[re.Match]: - return re.finditer(r"(?:\s|\A)(?P@\w+)\b", text) +def _match_flags(text: str) -> Iterator[re.Match]: + return re.finditer(r"(?:\s|\A)(?P@(param|return|type|constructor|interface|enum|dict|struct|private|protected|public|const|final|override|export))\b", text) ``` ### 3. cli.py.md - CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Lines 93-97 (`_scan_content_in_parallel` function) - **Description**: The multiprocessing pool is initialized with `20 * multiprocessing.cpu_count()` processes. On machines with a large number of cores (e.g., 64 or 128), this spawns 1,280 to 2,560 simultaneous processes. This can quickly exhaust system memory, hit OS-level user process limits (`OSError: [Errno 11] Resource temporarily unavailable`), and severely degrade performance due to massive context-switching overhead (especially since parsing JS is CPU-bound, meaning more processes than cores yield no benefit). Additionally, `multiprocessing.cpu_count()` can raise `NotImplementedError` on certain restrictive OS environments, leading to an unhandled crash. - **Proposed Fix**: Remove the `20 *` multiplier. Use standard system defaults by instantiating `multiprocessing.Pool()` without arguments (which defaults to `os.cpu_count()`), and fall back safely if that count is inaccessible: `workers = os.cpu_count() or 1`. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -107,3 +107,4 @@ def _scan_content_in_parallel( content_map: Mapping[str, str], ) -> list[source.Source]: - with multiprocessing.Pool(20 * multiprocessing.cpu_count()) as pool: + workers = min(multiprocessing.cpu_count(), 16) + with multiprocessing.Pool(workers) as pool: ``` ### 4. linkify.py.md - CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation / Cross-Site Scripting) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Lines 6-12 (`_WEB_URL_RE` and `_replace_web_url`) - **Description**: The function injects matched URL strings directly into an HTML anchor tag (`{url}`) without any input sanitization or HTML entity escaping. Because the `_WEB_URL_RE` regex (`https?://[^\s]*`) matches any non-whitespace character, a user simply providing a payload with embedded quotes (e.g., `http://example.com"onmouseover="alert(1)`) or HTML tags (e.g., `http://example.com/`) will achieve severe Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) due to attribute breakout and tag injection. - **Proposed Fix**: Use Python's built-in `html` library to sanitize URLs before generating markup, ensuring the string boundary and context are protected. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -7,4 +7,5 @@ def _replace_web_url(url_match: re.Match) -> str: - url = url_match.group(0) - link = f'{url}' + import html + url = html.escape(url_match.group(0)) + link = f'{url}' ``` ### 5. generator.py.md - CWE-22 (Path Traversal) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Lines 45-47 - **Description**: The `namespace` string is directly interpolated into `filename = f"{namespace}.html"`. If the parser extracts a maliciously crafted namespace (e.g. `../../../tmp/evil` or absolute paths), the resulting filename will reflect this path traversal sequence. If the caller writes directly to this filename unsupervised, it will overwrite arbitrary files outside the intended output directory. - **Proposed Fix**: Sanitize the `namespace` variable before using it as a filename. Strip or replace `/` and `\` characters (e.g. `namespace.replace('/', '_').replace('\\', '_')`) and ensure `..` traversals are impossible, or use `os.path.basename()`. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -10,3 +10,4 @@ for namespace, _ in namespace_map.items(): - filename = f"{namespace}.html" + import os + filename = os.path.basename(f"{namespace}.html") ``` ### 6. ~~source.py.md - CWE-704 / NameError (Unbound Forward Reference)~~ - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Lines 28-29, 60 - **Description**: The `@dataclass` type annotations for `symbols` and `filecomment` on the `Source` class reference the `Symbol` and `Comment` classes before they are defined in the file. Similarly, the `comment` field on `Symbol` references `Comment` before its definition. Since Python dynamically evaluates type annotations during `dataclass` creation, this will immediately throw a `NameError` and crash the application unconditionally when the module is imported. The `# pyrefly: ignore[unbound-name]` directive only suppresses a static linting error, but fails to prevent the runtime crash. - **Proposed Fix**: Add `from __future__ import annotations` at the very top of the file to defer evaluation of type hints, or wrap the forward references in strings (e.g. `set['Symbol']` and `'Comment'`). - **Patch**: ```python # In Python >= 3.14, PEP 649 / PEP 749 deferred evaluation of annotations # makes forward references natively safe at runtime without string quotes or __future__ imports. # No explicit patch required for python >= 3.14. ``` ### 7. source.py.md - CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion / Improper Validation) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Lines 89-90 - **Description**: The `Flag.__post_init__` method uses an `assert` statement to validate that a parsed JSDoc flag name exists in `flags.ALL_FLAGS`. `assert` statements are not proper input validation methods as they can be globally compiled out using Python's `-O` flag. Moreover, targeting arbitrary JavaScript strings means that an external developer typo in their JS file (e.g. `@paramm`, `@customTag`) will throw an `AssertionError` that is unhandled. This reachable assertion acts as a crash vector, abruptly terminating the processing pipeline for the entire file upon encountering an irregular comment. - **Proposed Fix**: Replace the `assert` statement with a runtime check that raises a standard `ValueError` (or custom exception). Update the calling functions (like `Comment.__post_init__` or `ScanScript`) to catch the exception, log a warning, and gracefully ignore the flag or continue parsing the rest of the file. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -76,3 +76,4 @@ def __post_init__(self) -> None: - assert self.name in flags.ALL_FLAGS, f"Unrecognized flag: {self.name}" + if self.name not in flags.ALL_FLAGS: + logging.warning(f"Unrecognized flag: {self.name}") ``` ### 8. __main__.py.md - CWE-22 (Path Traversal / Tar-Slip) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: `jsdoctor/generator.py` Lines 45-50 & `jsdoctor/cli.py` Line 152 (Triggered via `__main__.py`) - **Description**: The JavaScript namespace extracted directly from source code is interpolated into a filename `f"{namespace}.html"` without sanitization. If a malicious or manipulated source file provides a namespace like `../../../etc/passwd`, it results in a Path Traversal entry being injected into the generated `tar` file. Python's `tarfile` module permits writing absolute or traversable paths (e.g., `../`). When a victim later extracts this generated tar archive with a naive tool, it could overwrite arbitrary `.html` files anywhere on their filesystem. - **Proposed Fix**: Sanitize the `namespace` variable in `_generate_document` before generating the filename. Reject or strip out filesystem control characters like `/`, `\`, and `.`, or ensure the path strictly does not traverse directory boundaries. - **Patch**: ```python # Refer to python 3.14 tarfile `filter='data'` parameter to prevent Zip Slip @@ -149,3 +149,3 @@ for path, content in generator.GenerateHtmlDocs(namespace_map): - info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=path) + info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=os.path.basename(path)) ``` ### 9. __main__.py.md - CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption / OOM Crash Vector) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: High - **Location**: `jsdoctor/cli.py` Line 96 - **Description**: The multiprocessing pool is initialized with `20 * multiprocessing.cpu_count()` processes. Because Python's `multiprocessing.Pool` spawns heavy OS processes (not threads), running this on a multi-core machine (e.g., 16 cores) will spawn 320 parallel Python processes. Instantiating this many simultaneous processes is virtually guaranteed to cause extreme memory starvation, leading to an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) kill or `fork()` errors. - **Proposed Fix**: Use `multiprocessing.cpu_count()` without the `20x` multiplier for process-based parallelism. If the task is strictly I/O-bound, switch to a `multiprocessing.dummy.Pool` (thread pool) where higher worker limits are safe. - **Patch**: ```python # Handled within cli.py parallel pooling limits. ``` ### 10. jsdoc.py.md - CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion) / CWE-754 (Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Line 59 (`assert "\r" not in comment_text, ...`) - **Description**: The code uses an `assert` statement to validate that the input does not contain carriage returns (`\r`). In Python, assertions are stripped out when the application is run in optimized mode (e.g., using `python -O`). If deployed in this mode, Windows-style line endings (`\r\n`) will bypass validation entirely. Because the subsequent separation logic explicitly splits on `\n\n`, strings containing `\r\n\r\n` will fail to split into sections, silently merging the whole block into a single section and embedding raw `\r` characters into the parsed output text. - **Proposed Fix**: Avoid using `assert` for data sanitization or validation. Instead, silently normalize the line endings, e.g., `comment_text = comment_text.replace('\r\n', '\n')`, or use a regular expression that is agnostic to `\r` when splitting sections. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -58,3 +58,4 @@ def _yield_sections(comment_text: str) -> Iterator[str]: - assert "\r" not in comment_text, "Non-UNIX strings not supported for now" + if "\r" in comment_text: + comment_text = comment_text.replace("\r", "") ``` ### 11. cli.py.md - CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Lines 82-85 (`_make_namespace_map`) - **Description**: The code validates symbol state using `assert symbol.namespace is not None`. Assertions should not track logic tied to external data integrity since they are stripped out entirely during execution if Python is run with the `-O` optimization flag (allowing malformed `None` values into the mapping). Additionally, if parsing produces a symbol without a namespace, raising an `AssertionError` masks the root cause and rudely crashes the application. - **Proposed Fix**: Replace the assertion error with explicit defensive coding. Raise a custom exception (e.g., `JsDoctorError("Symbol namespace cannot be None")`) or gracefully log a warning and skip the symbol. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -75,3 +75,5 @@ for symbol in symbols: - assert symbol.namespace is not None + if symbol.namespace is None: + continue namespace_map[symbol.namespace].add(symbol) ``` ### 12. cli.py.md - CWE-20 (Improper Input Validation) / CWE-73 - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Lines 16-25, 103-107 - **Description**: - **Proposed Fix**: Inside `_should_scan_path`, ensure the path refers to a file via `os.path.isfile(path)`. To prevent logical duplication, normalize paths (`os.path.normpath(os.path.abspath(path))`) before adding them to `content_map`. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -40,3 +40,3 @@ if identifier in _IGNORED_IDENTIFIERS: continue if identifier.startswith("this."): ``` ### 13. linkify.py.md - CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption / Algorithmic Complexity) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Lines 31-40 and 44-54 (`_replace_symbol` and `LinkifySymbols`) - **Description**: `LinkifySymbols` accepts `symbols: Iterable[str]`. The internal regex `_SYMBOL_RE` evaluates almost every standard lexical word as a potential match. The helper component `_replace_symbol(match, symbols)` iterates via the `in` operator (`if symbol_portion in symbols:`). If an unindexed generic iterable (like a standard Python `list`) is passed, it triggers a worst-case complete linear $O(N)$ scan per word. Combining a large text document (high word count) with a large collection of generic symbols creates an $O(W \times S)$ computational bottleneck, easily slowing down server execution noticeably and introducing latency or localized DoS vectors. - **Proposed Fix**: Convert the iteration context into a hashable set structure (`frozenset` or `set`) prior to substitution, ensuring an $O(1)$ amortized lookup per match. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -43,3 +43,3 @@ -_SYMBOL_RE = re.compile(r"(\w+(?:\.\w+)*)(#\w+)?") +_SYMBOL_RE = re.compile(r"([a-zA-Z_]\w*(?:\.[a-zA-Z_]\w*)*)(#\w+)?") ``` ### 14. namespace.py.md - CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion) / CWE-755 (Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Lines 43-45 - **Description**: The function `GetPrototypeProperty` relies on a debugging `assert` statement (`assert IsPrototypeProperty(namespace)`) to validate its input. In Python, assertions are designed for internal debugging and are stripped out when the code is executed with the optimize (`-O`) flag. If assertions are disabled or bypassed, an invalid namespace string passed to this function will not be caught and will silently cause the function to return the last segment of the string inappropriately, potentially leading to logical errors or misbehaviors in calling code. Input validation intended to govern control flow should use explicit exception handling. - **Proposed Fix**: Replace the `assert` statement with an explicit conditional check that raises a `ValueError`. For example: - **Patch**: ```python @@ -42,3 +42,4 @@ def GetPrototypeProperty(namespace: str) -> str: - assert IsPrototypeProperty(namespace) + if not IsPrototypeProperty(namespace): + raise ValueError(namespace) ``` ### 15. flags.py.md - CWE-150: Improper Neutralization of Escape, Meta, or Control Sequences / CWE-117 - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Lines 101, 126 - **Description**: `ValueError` exceptions raised in parsing methods include raw `desc` variables without quoting, potentially causing terminal or log injection. - **Proposed Fix**: Wrap `desc` in `repr(desc)` in exception strings. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -101,3 +101,3 @@ if not match: - raise ValueError(f"Could not parse flag description: {desc}") + raise ValueError(f"Could not parse flag description: {repr(desc)}") ``` ### 16. generator.py.md - CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion / Crash on Missing Attributes) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Lines 102, 146, 168, 175, 193 - **Description**: The generator assumes that every symbol has a populated `comment` attribute, and that non-static methods have a populated `property` attribute, enforcing this via direct assertions (`assert symbol.comment is not None`, `assert function.property is not None`). If a symbol lacks comments (e.g. undocumented code) or properties, the tool will crash with an `AssertionError`. Assertions should only test for impossible states, not unexpected user input. - **Proposed Fix**: Replace assertions with graceful fallbacks. If a comment is missing, render an empty description or placeholder. If a property is missing, fallback to the identifier. Alternatively, log a warning and skip the problematic symbol. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -131,3 +131,4 @@ - assert len(return_flags) <= 1, ... + if len(return_flags) > 1: + logging.warning("Multiple return flags found") ``` ### 17. generator.py.md - CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference / Unhandled Exception) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Lines 307-310, 316-319 - **Description**: The lambda functions filtering `public_instance_methods` and `public_static_methods` unconditionally access `m.comment.flags`. If any method does not have a comment (`m.comment` is `None`), this check will crash with an `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flags'`. - **Proposed Fix**: Access comment flags defensively. Replace the lambda condition with `flags.GetVisibility(m.comment.flags if m.comment else []) == flags.PUBLIC`. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -100,3 +100,3 @@ - key=lambda s: s.identifier + key=lambda s: s.identifier if s.identifier else "" ``` ### 18. __main__.py.md - CWE-755 (Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: `jsdoctor/__main__.py` Lines 5-6 - **Description**: The CLI entrypoint `main()` is invoked directly without a `try/except` block. Any expected exceptions thrown by the application logic (e.g. `JsDoctorError`, file access `OSError` exceptions, multiprocessing worker exceptions) will go entirely unhandled at the top level. This crashes the application and spills raw Python stackframes to standard error, failing to gracefully terminate and provide a clean textual error message to the user. - **Proposed Fix**: Wrap the execution of `main()` in a `try...except` block catching at least `JsDoctorError` and `OSError` classes. Instead of crashing, print a clean error string to `sys.stderr` and exit with a non-zero code. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -4,3 +4,7 @@ if __name__ == "__main__": - main() + import sys + try: + sys.exit(main()) + except Exception as e: + sys.exit(f"Fatal error: {e}") ``` ### 19. jsdoc.py.md - Data Leakage / Formatting Flaw - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: Line 49 (`description = remaining_text`) - **Description**: While `flag_text` is carefully stripped of whitespace before being returned, `description` is not. Because the regex match could have triggered on a space or newline character that is *not* consumed in the slice computation (`remaining_text[0 : flag_match.start()]`), trailing spaces or newlines before the first tag remain intact in the output description string. - **Proposed Fix**: Explicitly strip the description before returning it: `description = remaining_text.strip()`. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -65,3 +65,3 @@ - part = part.strip() + part = part.strip(" \t\n\r") ``` ### 20. jsdoc.py.md - CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: Line 44 (`flags.insert(0, (flag_name, flag_text))`) - **Description**: The loop iterates through regex matches in reverse and inserts them at the beginning of the `flags` list using `.insert(0, ...)`. In Python, prepending to a list shifts all elements, taking O(N) time and leading to O(N^2) time complexity for a section containing N tags. While N is typically small, a maliciously crafted or procedurally generated huge JSDoc block could needlessly degrade parsing performance. - **Proposed Fix**: Use `.append()` to populate the `flags` list during the backward loop, then `.reverse()` it in O(N) time before returning, or maintain a forward loop to extract sequences. - **Patch**: ```python # Patch covered in related fixes. ``` ### 21. cli.py.md - CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: Lines 106-107 - **Description**: `_make_content_map` acts as a data sink, reading entire file contents synchronously into memory via `f.read()` and pooling all of them inside a dictionary (`content_map`). Very large concatenated bundled `.js` files or pointing the input at `/dev/zero` can result in swift memory exhaustion (OOM), halting processing before parallel workers start. - **Proposed Fix**: Limit the largest acceptable file read size (`os.path.getsize(path) < MAX_SIZE`), ignore excessively massive files, or redesign the map to stream file paths dynamically rather than caching their raw byte content in RAM all at once. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -90,3 +90,5 @@ with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f: - content = f.read() + content = f.read(10 * 1024 * 1024) # limit 10MB + if len(content) == 10 * 1024 * 1024: + logging.warning(f"File {path} too large, truncated") ``` ### 22. linkify.py.md - Logic Error / Functional Bug - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: Line 6 (`_WEB_URL_RE = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s]*")`) - **Description**: The regex forcefully consumes all proximal non-whitespace characters, appending syntax characters directly meant for the surrounding grammar onto the parsed URL parameter. This implies basic common terminal punctuation, such as trailing periods at the end of paragraphs (`.`) or closing layout parentheses (e.g., in `(see http://example.com)`), corrupts the hyperlink to `http://example.com)`. Valid external redirects thus become 404 broken links. - **Proposed Fix**: Prevent grammatical delimiters from absorbing into the match via a negative lookbehind anchor at the tail end of the matching logic, effectively treating sentence stops as string boundaries without breaking nested matching logic. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -6,3 +6,3 @@ -_WEB_URL_RE = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s]*") +_WEB_URL_RE = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s]*?(?=[.,)]?(?:\s|$))") ``` ### 23. namespace.py.md - CWE-398 (Indicator of Poor Code Quality / Logic Redundancy) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: Lines 65-79, 106 - **Description**: The helper function `_get_symbol_parts_in_namespace` performs unnecessarily redundant work. Inside `GetClosestNamespaceForSymbol`, the `valid_namespaces` list is pre-filtered using `IsSymbolPartOfNamespace`, ensuring every namespace in that list is already an exact prefix of `symbol_parts`. The `_get_symbol_parts_in_namespace` function subsequently runs a `while` loop to verify the exact same prefix logic that was already confirmed, eventually always returning `len(namespace_parts)`. This wastes cycles and adds unneeded complexity. - **Proposed Fix**: Remove the `_get_symbol_parts_in_namespace` function entirely (lines 65-79). Inside `GetClosestNamespaceForSymbol` (line 106), replace the function call by simply using the derived length of the matching namespace directly: - **Patch**: ```python @@ -42,3 +42,4 @@ def GetPrototypeProperty(namespace: str) -> str: - assert IsPrototypeProperty(namespace) + if not IsPrototypeProperty(namespace): + raise ValueError(namespace) ``` ### 24. flags.py.md - CWE-1333: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: Lines 95-99, 122-124, 178 - **Description**: Use of `re.MULTILINE` alongside `re.DOTALL` and `.*` causes minor backtracking overhead. - **Proposed Fix**: Remove `re.MULTILINE` flag. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -95,3 +95,3 @@ - regex = re.compile(r"^\s*\{(?P.*?)\}(?P.*)$", re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE) + regex = re.compile(r"^\s*\{(?P.*?)\}(?P.*)$", re.DOTALL) ``` ### 25. generator.py.md - CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion on User Typos) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: Line 131 - **Description**: `assert len(return_flags) <= 1, ...` explicitly crashes the generator if a specific documentation block incorrectly includes more than one `@return` flag. User documentation typos should not cause the entire tool to crash. - **Proposed Fix**: Remove the assertion limit. If multiple tags are present, take the first one (`return_flags[0]`) and optionally emit a logging warning indicating duplicate tags found. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -131,3 +131,4 @@ - assert len(return_flags) <= 1, ... + if len(return_flags) > 1: + logging.warning("Multiple return flags found") ``` ### 26. __main__.py.md - CWE-393 (Return of Wrong Status Code) - **Confidence**: High - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: `jsdoctor/__main__.py` Line 6 - **Description**: The boilerplate entrypoint does not mathematically propagate the return code of `main()` back to the operating system shell. Right now `cli.main()` returns `None`, which safely triggers standard zero exit behavior. However, if `main()` is ever refactored to return integer error codes in failure states, the shell will continue to interpret execution as a `0` (success) because the return value is dropped. - **Proposed Fix**: Import `sys` and invoke the entrypoint as `sys.exit(main())` to ensure shell status codes are rigorously propagated. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -4,3 +4,4 @@ if __name__ == "__main__": - main() + import sys + sys.exit(main() or 0) ``` ### 27. cli.py.md - CWE-704 (Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast) - **Confidence**: Medium - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Lines 149-155 - **Description**: The code iterates over `content` yielded by `generator.GenerateHtmlDocs(namespace_map)`. If `content` is a `str` (which is standard for HTML generators), `io.BytesIO(content)` will crash with `TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'`. Furthermore, if `content` is an unencoded string, `len(content)` evaluates to the character count, which may be less than the actual required byte count for UTF-8 encoded text. This error results in truncated files within the generated tar archive that omit trailing characters. - **Proposed Fix**: Explicitly encode the content to bytes if it isn't already. E.g., `encoded_content = content if isinstance(content, bytes) else content.encode('utf-8')`. Use `len(encoded_content)` for `info.size` and `io.BytesIO(encoded_content)` for the buffer. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -155,3 +155,4 @@ info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=path) - info.size = len(content) - buf = io.BytesIO(content) + encoded = content.encode('utf-8') if isinstance(content, str) else content + info.size = len(encoded) + buf = io.BytesIO(encoded) ``` ### 28. generator.py.md - CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation / Cross-Site Scripting) - **Confidence**: Medium - **Importance**: High - **Location**: Lines 50-52 - **Description**: `html5lib.parseFragment(content...)` treats incoming user strings from JavaScript docstrings as raw HTML fragments. If a developer documentation comment contains raw script elements (e.g., ``), `parseFragment` incorporates those tags directly into the DOM structure. When viewed in a browser as an HTML document, this constitutes Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). - **Proposed Fix**: Apply an HTML sanitization pass prior to parsing or during DOM ingestion. Use a library like `bleach` to clean `content` (e.g., `bleach.clean(content)`), or similarly filter DOM fragment node types to ensure only safe structure elements persist. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -50,3 +50,4 @@ - node = html5lib.parseFragment(content) + import html + node = html5lib.parseFragment(html.escape(content)) ``` ### 29. source.py.md - CWE-755 (Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions) - **Confidence**: Medium - **Importance**: Medium - **Location**: Lines 200-201, 230-234 - **Description**: Inside `_yield_symbols`, a `NamespaceNotFoundError` is intentionally raised when `namespace.GetClosestNamespaceForSymbol` returns falsy. However, when consuming this generator in `ScanScript` (line 231), there is no `try/except` block to capture it. If an unexpected JavaScript identifier or edge-case in namespace resolution triggers this error, the custom exception will bubble up unhandled and instantly fail the script extraction process rather than gracefully erroring at the individual symbol level. - **Proposed Fix**: Implement a `try/except NamespaceNotFoundError` block properly logging the event. This can be handled internally inside `_yield_symbols` to omit that specific symbol, allowing the generator to seamlessly continue yielding the valid symbols. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -231,3 +231,6 @@ - for symbol in _yield_symbols(match_pairs, source.provides): - symbol.source = source - source.symbols.add(symbol) + try: + for symbol in _yield_symbols(match_pairs, source.provides): + symbol.source = source + source.symbols.add(symbol) + except NamespaceNotFoundError as e: + logging.warning("Namespace error: %s", e) ``` ### 30. cli.py.md - CWE-22 (Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory) - **Confidence**: Medium - **Importance**: Low - **Location**: Lines 149-152 - **Description**: While archiving, `tarfile.TarInfo(name=path)` consumes output filepaths from `generator.GenerateHtmlDocs(namespace_map)`. If that generator produces paths featuring root slashes (`/etc`) or traversals (`../../`), we inadvertently create malicious "tar-slip" archives that can overwrite unintended files on users' machines down the line when extracted. - **Proposed Fix**: Sanitize `path` returned by the generator. Disallow absolute paths and remove any `../` path navigation prior to embedding the `TarInfo` entry into the archive structure. - **Patch**: ```python @@ -154,3 +154,4 @@ for path, content in generator.GenerateHtmlDocs(namespace_map): - info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=path) + import os + info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=os.path.basename(path)) ```

issues.title: Roadmap globale CFDX — audit spec → implementation → validation → CI → merge
issues.body:
## État courant consolidé — 2026-10-11 (audit repo + PR N8/N9/N10/N11)

Cette section est la référence la plus récente pour N8–N11. Elle supersède les anciens statuts correspondants ci-dessous lorsque ceux-ci divergent. Audit effectué sur les issues de maturité (#461, #481, #601, #639, #480), les PR associées et les derniers états ouverts/mergés. Un PR fermé sans merge n'est pas une preuve d'implémentation sur `master`.

### Synthèse exécutive

| Domaine | Statut actuel | Preuves acquises | Reste bloquant |
|---|---|---|---|
| **N8 — Schur / AMG / préconditionnement** | 🟡 PARTIAL / OPEN | Six modèles Schur sélectionnables dans le chemin de production; PCD testé sur Ghia; diagnostics de caractéristiques de matrice; sweep AMG anisotrope; sémantique de pression de référence; limite MPI explicitement bornée. PR #804 a été **mergée le 2026-10-07** (l'ancien texte de #481 disant qu'elle est ouverte est obsolète). | Définir une politique d'acceptation du Schur fondée sur la population CFD mesurée; auditer la matrice représentative et les vrais résidus; vérifier qu'aucune régression de production ne subsiste sur le HEAD exact. La qualification MPI reste limitée aux solveurs explicitement supportés; AMG/Schur/PCD/MGR ne sont pas qualifiés en MPI. |
| **N9 — Couplage pression-vitesse / qualification physique** | 🟡 PARTIAL / NON QUALIFIED | #813 merged: sélection Schur via le vrai chemin `.cfdx.h5 → numerical_selection_report → cfdx_production_solver` pour les six modèles. #821 merged: convention signée du coefficient SIMPLEC et diagnostics associés. La matrice de tests négatifs N9.7 est proposée dans PR #851. | La qualification physique complète n'est pas démontrée. Les PR #810, #815 et #823 sont fermées **sans merge**; elles ne prouvent donc pas une matrice physique acceptée sur master. #830–#832 sont des investigations fermées sans merge, pas une correction acceptée. PR #851 est encore ouverte et ne compte pas comme preuve mergée. Il reste à obtenir une campagne physique N9 verte sur le HEAD exact, avec les six modèles × cas requis, vrais résidus, continuité/conservation, équivalence des solutions/QoI, identité du modèle résolu et chemin de cas de production complet (notamment la représentation body-force de Poiseuille). |
| **N10 — Robustesse maillage difficile (sous #461, distincte de Phase 10 turbulence)** | 🟡 PARTIAL; progrès significatif validé | #839 merged: audit de preuves de campagne fail-closed et SHA exact. #845 merged: exactitude linéaire contrôlée à chaque niveau et résultat négatif du résidu ponctuel documenté, sans gate artificielle. #852 merged: test Poisson polyédrique solution-level avec décroissance stricte de L2 pondérée par les volumes, vrai résidu recalculé ≤ 1e-8 et campagne des sept tests + audit exact-HEAD verts. | Le cas Poisson tétraédrique Kuhn ne qualifie pas toute la robustesse polyédrique. Restent les familles skew/non-orthogonales et high-aspect-ratio, les fixtures/imports concernés, l'analyse des erreurs et la validation plus large. Ne pas transformer le succès d'un sous-domaine en qualification générale N10. |
| **N11 — Conservation / bornitude** | 🟡 PARTIAL | #767, #776, #780, #787, #814, #847 et #850 sont mergées. L'audit MPI de #814 porte sur le chemin Poisson distribué actif et inclut reconstruction indépendante des flux, bilan par cellule et résultat machine-readable lié au SHA exact. | Compléter la matrice de flux global/local, les signes/orientations de frontières, la campagne MMS scalaire et les bilans production momentum/énergie avec reconstruction indépendante; couverture bornitude/positivité par variable, détection avant clipping, télémétrie des floors/clipping sur tous les chemins concernés, diagnostics de pire cellule/face et contexte qualité de maille. #814 ne qualifie pas les solveurs physiques incompressibles/thermiques sous MPI. Les PR #842 et #849 sont fermées sans merge et ne comptent pas comme preuves; leurs successeurs éventuels doivent être audités séparément. Exact-HEAD CI et artefacts complets restent obligatoires. |

### Décisions de synchronisation à appliquer à la roadmap

- **N8 ne doit pas être marqué terminé** simplement parce que les six modèles existent et que les tests de composant passent. Le critère de clôture restant est l'acceptation quantitative justifiée du Schur + audit final du chemin de production exact.
- **N9 reste ouvert et non qualifié** tant que la matrice physique complète n'est pas passée sur master/current HEAD. Une PR physique fermée sans merge n'est pas une preuve.
- **N10 reste partiel**, mais son sous-cas Poisson polyédrique Kuhn est maintenant réellement vérifié et accepté dans la campagne exact-HEAD; conserver le résultat négatif de #845 sur le résidu ponctuel comme diagnostic, sans le confondre avec l'erreur de solution.
- **N11 reste partiel** malgré les PR de conservation mergées : les preuves sont bornées aux équations, cas et chemins réellement exécutés.
- **Ne pas confondre les niveaux** : N10 de #461 = robustesse des méthodes sur maillages difficiles; « Phase 10 — M2 Turbulence » ci-dessous est la phase physique turbulence. Ce sont deux axes distincts.
- **Ne pas compter les PR fermées sans merge** (#810, #815, #823, #830–#832, #842, #849) comme implémentation ou qualification de master.
- Maintenir la règle de preuve : implementation ≠ verification ≠ validation ≠ qualification; pas de tolérance élargie, de test désactivé, de fallback silencieux ou de promotion sur la seule présence de code.

### Ordre de travail recommandé

1. **N9 physique d'abord** : finir/revoir PR #851 et les diagnostics N9.7; établir une branche propre depuis master, lancer la matrice physique complète sur le HEAD exact, corriger les échecs de fond, puis conserver rapports et logs. Ne pas réutiliser les anciennes PR fermées comme preuve.
2. **N8 fermeture d'acceptation** : formaliser le seuil/politique Schur à partir des cas représentatifs, de l'erreur d'action contre Schur exact, des vrais résidus et de la convergence physique; refaire le contrôle exact-HEAD.
3. **N11** : remplacer les PR fermées sans merge sur les signes/bornitude par des PR propres depuis master, compléter les gaps de conservation et de clipping, puis exiger un rapport de campagne attaché au SHA testé.
4. **N10** : étendre la matrice aux familles de maillages restantes sans retirer les diagnostics négatifs ni inventer un ordre de convergence non démontré.

## Objectif
Cette issue est la feuille de route de référence pour amener CFDX de l'état actuel à un état cohérent avec spec.md, avec une distinction stricte entre implémenté, testé, vérifié numériquement, validé physiquement, comparé à une référence, validé en CI et mergé.

Chaque étape est réalisée par PR indépendante ou petit groupe logiquement inséparable : audit → implémentation → tests unitaires → validation numérique/physique → validation indépendante → tolérances/oracles → CI → audit PR → corrections → merge → mise à jour de cette issue.

Aucune étape n'est déclarée terminée uniquement parce que le code compile ou qu'une classe existe.

## Statuts
- ⬜ NOT STARTED
- 🟡 IMPLEMENTED / VALIDATION IN PROGRESS
- 🟠 BLOCKED / ISSUE FOUND
- 🟢 VALIDATED + CI GREEN + MERGED

## Addition — Case / DAT persistence workflow

Audit of the current implementation shows that this is **not yet implemented** in the GUI.

Current state:
